```ts
 * may ask the worker to delete. And every statement that locks or deletes several image rows takes them in id order, so
 * that no two transactions ever lock one post's images in opposite orders.
 */

export interface MediaRow {
  id: string;
  ownerId: string;
  status: "processing" | "ready" | "failed";
  error: string | null;
  postId: string | null;
  width: number | null;
  height: number | null;
  blurhash: string | null;
  createdAt: Date;
  /** The image's own moderation state, which only a migrator-owned function writes. A sealed image is shown to nobody. */
  moderationState: "visible" | "withheld" | "removed" | "sealed";
}

/** One hold request of an intake: a post whose images the case holds as evidence, or an account whose images are only locked. */
export type HoldPair = { caseId: string; postId: string } | { ownerId: string };

/** An image as a case's snapshot lists it. The alt text is null for an image whose content was erased. */
export interface HeldImage {
  id: string;
  alt: string | null;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}

/** What a case about a post or an account reaches: counts, a day and a time, never an id, an alt text or a file. */
export interface CaseReach {
  /** The posts the case reaches that have image rows. */
  posts: number;
  images: number;
  sealed: number;
  /** The images korbat's server would still give to some reader. */
  served: number;
  /** The creation day, in UTC, of the newest post with image rows. */
  newestPostOn: string | null;
  /** When the newest post with a served image was created. */
  newestServedAt: Date | null;
}

/** Ids as one uuid[] parameter. */
const uuidArray = (ids: readonly string[]): SQL => sql`${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]`;

/**
 * An image the data export hands its owner: ready, in a state its author still sees (a sealed image is exported to
 * nobody, and a state this reader has not been taught is left out), not erased, and either on no post or on a post that
 * is neither deleted, nor disabled for an authority's order, nor erased. A row that a case or a freeze kept after its
 * post was deleted is in no export. The query it is used in joins posts by the image's post.
 *
 * 3f (design, W.7 and 7.10): an order disables the post and leaves its images' own states as they were, so the post's
 * state is the only mark; the export leaves the files out as it leaves the post out, held notice or told.
 */
const EXPORTABLE = and(
  eq(postMedia.status, "ready"),
  inArray(postMedia.moderationState, ["visible", "withheld", "removed"]),
  isNull(postMedia.erasedAt),
  or(isNull(postMedia.postId), and(ne(posts.state, "deleted_by_author"), ne(posts.state, "disabled"), isNull(posts.erasedAt))),
);

/**
 * A row the disposal may take (3c design, section 7.9): nothing retains it (no hold stands, and its post is not frozen),
 * and its post is deleted, its owner is purged, or its post's content or its own was erased. `m` is the image row, `p`
 * its post when it has one, `o` its owner's profile. The freeze is read here only to keep kept rows out of a batch: for
 * each row that is deleted, post_media_keep decides.
 *
 * The marks and the freeze are one condition, a CASE that reads the freeze only for a row that carries a mark. As two
 * conditions the planner made the freeze the filter of the scan of post_media, since it names that table alone, and
 * called it for every attached image row in the table before any mark was tested: several index probes a row, seconds
 * for a table of thousands, however few rows were disposable. A CASE is evaluated in the order it is written, and this
 * one names all three tables, so it runs where they are joined.
 */
const DISPOSABLE = sql`(m.hold_until is null or m.hold_until <= now())
  and case when (p.state = 'deleted_by_author' or o.deleted_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null or m.erased_at is not null)
           then (m.post_id is null or not public.post_frozen(m.post_id))
           else false end`;

const columns = {
  id: postMedia.id,
  ownerId: postMedia.ownerId,
  status: postMedia.status,
  error: postMedia.error,
  postId: postMedia.postId,
  width: postMedia.width,
  height: postMedia.height,
  blurhash: postMedia.blurhash,
  createdAt: postMedia.createdAt,
  moderationState: postMedia.moderationState,
};

export function createMediaRepo(db: Db) {
  return {
    /** When the account was onboarded, which decides its upload tier. */
    async accountCreatedAt(userId: string): Promise<Date | null> {
      const rows = await db.select({ createdAt: profiles.createdAt }).from(profiles).where(eq(profiles.id, userId)).limit(1);
      return rows[0]?.createdAt ?? null;
    },

    /** Uploads of this account that are not on a post yet and did not fail. */
    async pendingCount(ownerId: string): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ count: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId), inArray(postMedia.status, ["processing", "ready"])));
      return rows[0]?.count ?? 0;
    },

    /**
     * The upload's row, as one statement that locks its owner's profile row FOR KEY SHARE and inserts only when the one
     * predicate holds (3e design, section 7.2): read in the statement that locks the row, by the clock. No row inserted
     * answers account_suspended, and the caller discards the received file. The statement's lock may wait for a holder
     * that only locks the row, which leaves its judgment as it was before the wait, so the transaction ends with the
     * closing judgment of the owner (3e's review): a deleted or suspended owner then rolls the insert back, answered
     * account_suspended as the statement answers both.
     */
    async insertProcessing(input: { id: string; ownerId: string; now: Date }): Promise<void> {
      await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const inserted = await tx.execute(sql`
          with ok as (select p.id from profiles p where p.id = ${input.ownerId}::uuid and ${liveNotSuspended("p", WRITE_CLOCK)} for key share of p)
          insert into post_media (id, owner_id, status, created_at)
          select ${input.id}::uuid, ok.id, 'processing', ${input.now.toISOString()}::timestamptz from ok
          returning id`);
        if (inserted.length === 0) throw new MediaError("account_suspended", 403);
        const judged = await closingJudgment(tx, input.ownerId);
        if (!judged || judged.deleted || judged.suspended) throw new MediaError("account_suspended", 403);
      });
    },

    /**
     * One image row, for its owner's status. Two rules of the readers hold here (3c design, section 7.10): a row that a
     * case or a freeze keeps after its post was deleted, and a row whose content, its own or its post's, was erased, is
     * answered as a row that does not exist, to its owner too, so nothing tells the author that the row was kept; and a
     * sealed image is handed over without its blurhash, which is made from the image.
     */
    async find(id: string): Promise<MediaRow | null> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ ...columns, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt, postState: posts.state, postErasedAt: posts.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(eq(postMedia.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      const found = rows[0];
      if (!found || found.postState === "deleted_by_author" || found.erasedAt !== null || found.postErasedAt !== null) return null;
      const { erasedAt: _erasedAt, postState: _postState, postErasedAt: _postErasedAt, ...row } = found;
      return row.moderationState === "sealed" ? { ...row, blurhash: null } : row;
    },

    /** Records the worker's verdict, once. A row that is no longer processing is left as it is. */
    async finalize(id: string, result: ResultFile): Promise<boolean> {
      const values = result.status === "ready" ? { status: "ready" as const, width: result.width, height: result.height, blurhash: result.blurhash } : { status: "failed" as const, error: result.reason };
      const rows = await db.update(postMedia).set(values).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.status, "processing"))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /** Removes an upload of this account that is not on a post. */
    async deleteUnattached(id: string, ownerId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /**
     * What serving an image file depends on: whether it is ready, its own moderation state, its post's state and author,
     * and whether its content or its post's was erased.
     */
    async fileAccess(id: string): Promise<{ status: MediaRow["status"]; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; postState: string | null; authorId: string | null; erased: boolean } | null> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ status: postMedia.status, mediaState: postMedia.moderationState, postState: posts.state, authorId: posts.authorId, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt, postErasedAt: posts.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(eq(postMedia.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      const found = rows[0];
      if (!found) return null;
      return { status: found.status, mediaState: found.mediaState, postState: found.postState, authorId: found.authorId, erased: found.erasedAt !== null || found.postErasedAt !== null };
    },

    /**
     * Puts images on a post, inside the transaction that creates it. Each must belong to the author,
     * be ready and be on no post yet; anything else rolls the post back.
     */
    async attach(tx: DbTx, input: { postId: string; ownerId: string; items: readonly { id: string; alt: string }[] }): Promise<void> {
      for (const [position, item] of input.items.entries()) {
        const rows = await tx
          .update(postMedia)
          .set({ postId: input.postId, position, altText: item.alt })
          .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, item.id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, input.ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId), eq(postMedia.status, "ready")))
          .returning({ id: postMedia.id });
        if (rows.length !== 1) throw new MediaError("media_unavailable", 400);
      }
    },

    /**
     * Removes a post's images, inside the transaction that deletes it, and says which files to delete afterwards. The
     * rows are taken in id order, under row locks, with no filter of its own: the keep trigger skips every row a case
     * holds and every row of a frozen post, and RETURNING omits them, so no file of a kept row is asked for. A plain
     * delete by post takes the rows in its scan's order, and deadlocked with an intake that locks the same rows by id.
     */
    async detachAll(tx: DbTx, postId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where post_id = ${postId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Removes every image row of the owner, on a post or not, whatever its state, inside the transaction
     * that purges the account, and says which files to delete afterwards (1b design, section 7.6). In id order under
     * row locks and with no filter, as detachAll: the keep trigger decides which rows stay.
     */
    async purgeOwner(tx: DbTx, ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * The images of a page of posts, in one query, in their order on each post, each with its own moderation state:
     * what the state means for a reader is the view builder's to say. A sealed image is its id and its state only:
     * nobody is given its size, its blurhash, its alt text or a path. An image of a deleted post, and one whose content
     * or whose post's was erased, is given to nobody, its owner included, so no view and no export names a row that a
     * case or a freeze kept. A state this reader has not been taught is left out.
     */
    async forPosts(postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostImage[]>> {
      const byPost = new Map<string, PostImage[]>();
      if (postIds.length === 0) return byPost;
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, width: postMedia.width, height: postMedia.height, blurhash: postMedia.blurhash, altText: postMedia.altText, state: postMedia.moderationState })
        .from(postMedia)
        .innerJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(inArray(postMedia.postId, [...postIds]), eq(postMedia.status, "ready"), ne(posts.state, "deleted_by_author"), isNull(postMedia.erasedAt), isNull(posts.erasedAt)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.postId, postMedia.position);
      for (const row of rows) {
        if (!row.postId) continue;
        let image: PostImage;
        if (row.state === "sealed") image = { id: row.id, state: "sealed" };
        else if (row.state === "visible" || row.state === "withheld" || row.state === "removed") {
          if (row.width === null || row.height === null || row.blurhash === null) continue;
          image = { id: row.id, state: row.state, width: row.width, height: row.height, blurhash: row.blurhash, alt: row.altText ?? "", small: mediaPath(row.id, "small"), large: mediaPath(row.id, "large") };
        } else {
          // A state added later does not compile until this reader says who is given it.
          const unknown: never = row.state;
          void unknown;
          continue;
        }
        byPost.set(row.postId, [...(byPost.get(row.postId) ?? []), image]);
      }
      return byPost;
    },

    /**
     * Every image of the account that the data export takes a file for, on a post or not, oldest first: the ready ones
     * the account still sees (EXPORTABLE). A withheld or removed image stays with its author; a sealed image, an image
     * of a deleted post and an erased one are exported to nobody.
     */
    async readyImages(ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .orderBy(postMedia.createdAt, postMedia.id);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Whether readyImages would still list this image of the owner: the export reads the row again when it opens each
     * file, so an image that was sealed, erased or deleted with its post while the archive streams is left out of it.
     */
    async isExportable(ownerId: string, id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .limit(1);
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /** Uploads that still wait for the worker's verdict. */
    async processingIds(): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db.select({ id: postMedia.id }).from(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.status, "processing")).orderBy(postMedia.createdAt);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /** Fails uploads the worker has not answered since `before`, and says which. */
    async failStale(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(postMedia)
        .set({ status: "failed", error: "processing_failed" })
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.status, "processing"), lt(postMedia.createdAt, before)))
        .returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /** Removes uploads made before `before` that were never put on a post, whatever their state, and says which. */
    async deleteUnattachedBefore(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(isNull(postMedia.postId), lt(postMedia.createdAt, before))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Which of these ids have a row, whatever the row's state: the reconcile pass asks it which stored files belong to
     * no row, so a row that a hold or a freeze keeps must be seen here, or its files would be swept as orphans.
     */
    async existing(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
      if (ids.length === 0) return new Set();
      const rows = await db.select({ id: postMedia.id }).from(postMedia).where(inArray(postMedia.id, [...ids]));
      return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.id));
    },

    /** Removes a row whatever its state. Used when an upload could not be handed to the worker. */
    async deleteRow(id: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ what moderation cases need

    /**
     * An intake's holds (3c design, sections 5 and 7.1, step 4), inside the intake's transaction. First one statement
     * locks, FOR KEY SHARE and in one id order, every image row the pairs name: the rows of each post and, for an owner
     * pair, every row of that owner that is on a post (an attached row's owner is its post's author, so those are the
     * images of the account's posts). The posts are read there, never locked. The lock is what makes a delete that races
     * the intake wait and then read the intake's committed item; a row whose delete committed first is not returned.
     * Then, for the post pairs only, the case's hold goes on each returned row that has no unreleased hold from that case
     * and is not erased, in id order, which is the order the holds are released in: an owner pair gets no hold, since the
     * images of a frozen post are kept whether a hold stands or not. It answers, for each post pair, the post's images
     * in position order, an erased one without its alt text; an empty list means the images are gone.
     */
    async hold(tx: DbTx, pairs: readonly HoldPair[]): Promise<Map<string, HeldImage[]>> {
      const caseOf = new Map<string, string>();
      const owners: string[] = [];
      for (const pair of pairs) {
        if ("postId" in pair) caseOf.set(pair.postId, pair.caseId);
        else owners.push(pair.ownerId);
      }
      const held = new Map<string, HeldImage[]>([...caseOf.keys()].map((postId) => [postId, []]));
      if (caseOf.size === 0 && owners.length === 0) return held;

      const locked = (await tx.execute(sql`
        select m.id, m.post_id, m.position, m.width, m.height, m.alt_text, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.post_id = any(${uuidArray([...caseOf.keys()])}) or m.owner_id = any(${uuidArray(owners)})
        order by m.id for key share of m`)) as unknown as { id: string; post_id: string; position: number; width: number; height: number; alt_text: string | null; erased: boolean }[];

      // The rows came back in id order; the holds are placed in that order too.
      const toHold = locked.filter((row) => caseOf.has(row.post_id) && !row.erased);
      if (toHold.length > 0) {
        await tx.execute(sql`
          insert into media_holds (media_id, case_id)
          select v.media_id, v.case_id
          from unnest(${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => row.id))}, ${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => caseOf.get(row.post_id)!))}) as v(media_id, case_id)
          where not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = v.media_id and h.case_id = v.case_id and h.released_at is null)
          order by v.media_id`);
      }

      for (const row of [...locked].sort((a, b) => a.position - b.position)) {
        held.get(row.post_id)?.push({ id: row.id, alt: row.erased ? null : (row.alt_text ?? ""), width: row.width, height: row.height });
      }
      return held;
    },

    /**
     * What a case about this post or this account reaches (3c design, section 6.1): the post itself, or every post
     * whose author is the account, whatever its state. One statement that locks nothing.
     */
    async reach(target: { type: "post" | "account"; id: string }): Promise<CaseReach> {
      // 3f (design, section 7.10): no reader serves an image of a post disabled for an order, whatever the image's own state.
      const served = sql`m.moderation_state <> 'sealed' and p.state <> 'deleted_by_author' and p.state::text <> 'disabled' and m.erased_at is null and p.erased_at is null`;
      const reached = target.type === "post" ? sql`m.post_id = ${target.id}::uuid` : sql`p.author_id = ${target.id}::uuid`;
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(distinct m.post_id)::int as posts,
               count(*)::int as images,
               (count(*) filter (where m.moderation_state = 'sealed'))::int as sealed,
               (count(*) filter (where ${served}))::int as served,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as newest_post_on,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) filter (where ${served}) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as newest_served_at
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${reached}`)) as unknown as { posts: number; images: number; sealed: number; served: number; newest_post_on: string | null; newest_served_at: string | null }[];
      return {
        posts: row!.posts,
        images: row!.images,
        sealed: row!.sealed,
        served: row!.served,
        newestPostOn: row!.newest_post_on,
        newestServedAt: row!.newest_served_at === null ? null : new Date(row!.newest_served_at),
      };
    },

    /**
     * What opening an image for staff depends on, in one query: the row with its post, its size and its own state,
     * whether its content or its post's was erased, and whether its post is frozen now. Null when no row has the id or
     * the image is on no post.
     */
    async staffAccess(id: string): Promise<{ postId: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean } | null> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select m.post_id, m.status, m.width, m.height, m.moderation_state, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased, public.post_frozen(m.post_id) as frozen
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.id = ${id}::uuid`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; moderation_state: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean }[];
      if (!row) return null;
      return { postId: row.post_id, status: row.status, width: row.width, height: row.height, mediaState: row.moderation_state, erased: row.erased, frozen: row.frozen };
    },

    /**
     * A page of the image rows that are on a post, in id order after `afterId` (from the start when it is null): each
     * one's id, its post, its stored moderation state and when its content was erased. It locks nothing and gives nothing
     * of an image itself. The staff command line's text-verify reads every such row through it, a page at a time, to
     * hold the stored states to what the ledger of measures says they must be.
     */
    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.4): the post an image's address belongs to, or null when no attached image row has the id. An
     * order that names a picture's address names its post; this is a read, and it holds no row.
     */
    async imagePost(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, mediaId: string): Promise<string | null> {
      const [row] = await q.select({ postId: postMedia.postId }).from(postMedia).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, mediaId), isNotNull(postMedia.postId))).limit(1);
      return row?.postId ?? null;
    },

    /** 3f (design, section 7.5): how many image rows each of these posts holds, for an order's screen; a post with none is left out. */
    async imageCounts(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, number>> {
      if (postIds.length === 0) return new Map();
      const found = await q
        .select({ postId: postMedia.postId, count: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(inArray(postMedia.postId, [...postIds]))
        .groupBy(postMedia.postId);
      return new Map(found.map((row) => [row.postId!, row.count]));
    },

    /**
     * 3f (design, sections 5 and 7.11): a post's image rows as staff.js order-access prints them for a preserved post: the
     * id, the pixel size and when the row was made, in position order. The table holds no digest of a file, and no file
     * is opened here.
     */
    async preservedImages(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, postId: string): Promise<{ id: string; width: number | null; height: number | null; createdAt: Date }[]> {
      return q
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, width: postMedia.width, height: postMedia.height, createdAt: postMedia.createdAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(eq(postMedia.postId, postId))
        .orderBy(postMedia.position, postMedia.id);
    },

    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.14): for each post a seal lists (seal_posts), the ids of its image rows now, in their order.
     * Read-only, through the caller's transaction; handover-list compares their number with what the seal recorded.
     */
    async sealImageRows(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">, sealActionId: string): Promise<{ postId: string; mediaIds: string[] }[]> {
      const found = await q.execute<{ post_id: string; media_id: string | null }>(
        sql`select s.post_id, m.id as media_id from public.seal_posts s left join public.post_media m on m.post_id = s.post_id
             where s.action_id = ${sealActionId}::uuid order by s.post_id, m.position, m.id`,
      );
      const byPost = new Map<string, string[]>();
      for (const row of found) {
        const ids = byPost.get(row.post_id) ?? [];
        if (row.media_id !== null) ids.push(row.media_id);
        byPost.set(row.post_id, ids);
      }
      return [...byPost].map(([postId, mediaIds]) => ({ postId, mediaIds }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d (design, sections 6.1 and 7.1): whether a file of the image is in the quarantine without an end (it is being
     * restored), and whether one is recorded as lost, through the two functions the API's role may call; the table itself
     * is closed to it. Asked only for a visible image whose file is missing from the store.
     */
    async custody(id: string): Promise<{ quarantined: boolean; lost: boolean }> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`select public.media_quarantined(${id}::uuid) as quarantined, public.media_lost(${id}::uuid) as lost`)) as unknown as { quarantined: boolean; lost: boolean }[];
      return { quarantined: row!.quarantined, lost: row!.lost };
    },

    /**
     * 3d: up to `limit` images whose files the quarantine's record says are lost and whose author is owed the notice
     * (lost_untold), the earliest first, each with its owner and its post's creation time when the image row and the post
     * are still there (null otherwise: nobody is left to tell).
     */
    async lostUntold(limit: number): Promise<{ mediaId: string; lostAt: Date; ownerId: string | null; postCreatedAt: Date | null }[]> {
      const found = (await db.execute(sql`
        select l.media_id, l.lost_at, m.owner_id, p.created_at as post_created_at
          from public.lost_untold(${limit}) l
          left join post_media m on m.id = l.media_id
          left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
         order by l.lost_at, l.media_id`)) as unknown as { media_id: string; lost_at: Date | string; owner_id: string | null; post_created_at: Date | string | null }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ mediaId: row.media_id, lostAt: new Date(row.lost_at), ownerId: row.owner_id, postCreatedAt: row.post_created_at === null ? null : new Date(row.post_created_at) }));
    },

    /** 3d: records the outcome of a lost image's notice (lost_told), which changes the image's rows only from pending. */
    async lostTold(mediaId: string, outcome: "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "none" | "failed"): Promise<void> {
      await db.execute(sql`select public.lost_told(${mediaId}::uuid, ${outcome}::delivery_state)`);
    },

    /**
     * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 7.1 and 8.10): quarantine_plan() as staff.js quarantine-list reads it, through the caller's
     * transaction, which reads as the migrator (the function is executable by nobody else). For each image of the plan:
     * its direction, its post (the image row's, or for an image row that is gone the post its quarantine rows recorded),
     * the names of its files whose rows have no end, and of those whose rows are neither returned nor destroyed (a lost
     * file is among them: there is nothing of it to move).
     */
    async quarantinePlan(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ direction: string; mediaId: string; postId: string | null; open: string[]; kept: string[] }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select p.direction, p.media_id,
               coalesce(m.post_id, (select min(f.post_id::text)::uuid from public.quarantine_files f where f.media_id = p.media_id)) as post_id,
               coalesce((select array_agg(f.file order by f.file) from public.quarantine_files f
                          where f.media_id = p.media_id and f.returned_at is null and f.destroyed_at is null and f.lost_at is null), '{}') as open,
               coalesce((select array_agg(f.file order by f.file) from public.quarantine_files f
                          where f.media_id = p.media_id and f.returned_at is null and f.destroyed_at is null), '{}') as kept
          from public.quarantine_plan() p
          left join post_media m on m.id = p.media_id
         order by p.direction, p.media_id`)) as unknown as { direction: string; media_id: string; post_id: string | null; open: string[]; kept: string[] }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ direction: row.direction, mediaId: row.media_id, postId: row.post_id, open: row.open, kept: row.kept }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d: for every post sealed for good (a seal_media in force whose decision is not interim) and not released (Task 2:
     * a released post's rows are erased and then dropped by the disposal, while its seal still lists it), its image rows
     * now, erased or not, and the counts that each such seal recorded for it in seal_posts, which quarantine-list compares.
     * Through the caller's transaction.
     */
    async sealedForGoodCounts(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ postId: string; rows: number; images: number[] }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select s.post_id, array_agg(distinct s.images::int) as images,
               (select count(*)::int from post_media m where m.post_id = s.post_id) as rows
          from public.seal_posts s join public.measures_in_force f on f.id = s.action_id
         where f.kind = 'seal_media' and f.decision_kind <> 'interim'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.release_posts r where r.post_id = s.post_id)
         group by s.post_id
         order by s.post_id`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; rows: number; images: number[] }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ postId: row.post_id, rows: row.rows, images: row.images }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 2 (sections 5 and 8.10): text-verify's first read of the release. The images of the quarantine whose file
     * still lies there (a row without an end), not marked unknown, whose image row is gone and whose post is not released:
     * a file korbat holds of an image it no longer has, which no release accounts for. Through the caller's transaction,
     * which reads as the migrator: quarantine_files is closed to the API's role.
     */
    async quarantineOrphans(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ mediaId: string; postId: string | null }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select f.media_id, min(f.post_id::text)::uuid as post_id from public.quarantine_files f
         where f.returned_at is null and f.destroyed_at is null and f.lost_at is null and not f.unknown and f.release_id is null
           and not exists (select 1 from post_media m where m.id = f.media_id)
           and not exists (select 1 from public.release_posts r where r.post_id = f.post_id)
         group by f.media_id order by f.media_id`)) as unknown as { media_id: string; post_id: string | null }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ mediaId: row.media_id, postId: row.post_id }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 2: text-verify's second read. The released posts that still hold an image row without erased_at: the release
     * erases every row of its posts in its own transaction, and a replay does the same, so such a row means a write around
     * them. Through the caller's transaction; the API's role reads both tables.
     */
    async releasedUnerased(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ postId: string; images: number }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select r.post_id, count(*)::int as images from public.release_posts r join post_media m on m.post_id = r.post_id
         where m.erased_at is null group by r.post_id order by r.post_id`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; images: number }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ postId: row.post_id, images: row.images }));
    },

    async moderationStates(afterId: string | null, limit: number): Promise<{ id: string; postId: string; moderationState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erasedAt: Date | null }[]> {
      const found = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, moderationState: postMedia.moderationState, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(isNotNull(postMedia.postId), afterId === null ? undefined : gt(postMedia.id, afterId)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.id)
        .limit(limit);
      return found.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, postId: row.postId!, moderationState: row.moderationState, erasedAt: row.erasedAt }));
    },

    /**
     * Deletes at most `limit` disposable rows (DISPOSABLE), the lowest ids first, inside the caller's transaction, and
     * answers the ids of the rows that are gone, in id order. The candidates are locked in id order inside the delete,
     * so the disposal and an intake's hold never lock one post's images in opposite orders; a candidate that another
     * transaction is making retained is waited for, checked again and skipped, and the batch is filled from the next ids.
     * The keep trigger decides for each row: a report that froze a candidate's post after this statement began is not
     * seen by its filter, and is seen by the trigger.
     *
     * The candidates are a materialized common table expression, which runs once. As a plain sub-select of the delete
     * they could run again for every row the delete looks at, when the planner joins the two by a nested loop: each run
     * skips the rows this statement has deleted already and lets the next ones in, so one call deleted more than its
     * limit (measured: 33 rows under a limit of 25).
     */
    async dropDisposable(tx: DbTx, limit: number): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(sql`
        with batch as materialized (
          select m.id
          from post_media m
          join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
          left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
          where ${DISPOSABLE}
          order by m.id
          limit ${limit}
          for update of m)
        delete from post_media where id in (select id from batch)
        returning id`)) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id).sort();
    },

    /**
     * How many rows the disposal should have taken by now: every disposable row none of whose holds ended, and none of
     * whose marks (its own erasure, its post's deletion or erasure) was set, within the last day. A hold ends when it is
     * released or when its time passes, whichever comes first. A row whose freeze ended within the last day may be
     * counted until the next round takes it: nothing records when a freeze ends.
     */
    async overdueDeletions(): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(*)::int as n
        from post_media m
        join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
        left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${DISPOSABLE}
          and not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = m.id and least(h.released_at, h.until) > now() - interval '1 day')
          and (m.erased_at is null or m.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.deleted_at is null or p.deleted_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.erased_at is null or p.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')`)) as unknown as { n: number }[];
      return row!.n;
    },
  };
}

export type MediaRepo = ReturnType<typeof createMediaRepo>;
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/moderation/alerts.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ALERT_KINDS, ALERT_RULES, PUSH_KINDS, type AlertChannelState, type AlertFacts, type AlertKind } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { StaffAlertKind, StaffMessage } from "../auth";
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { urgentWaiting } from "./repo";

/**
 * Staff alerts (3c design, section 7.12; 3f design, sections 5 and 7.2). Every alert has two legs. The push: one row of
 * alert_outbox, which the watcher (apps/api/src/notify) publishes to the phones with the fixed sentence of its kind,
 * counts and times only. The mail: to every live staff account, with counts and times and, for 3c's and 3e's kinds, the
 * staff handle where they name one; never a link or content. The moderation module, which never sees an address, keeps
 * each alert's throttle as one key of the shared limit store, and the alert tick below writes the time-driven alerts
 * (alert_steps()) and mails every 3f alert whose mail is its push's sentence, whoever wrote its row.
 */

/** The key and the window of the urgent lane's alert. The dispatch job repeats the alert under the same key. */
export const URGENT_ALERT_KEY = "moderation-urgent";
export const URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS = 15 * 60_000;

/** The alert tick's name: its lock is `job:alert-tick`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const ALERT_TICK_JOB = "alert-tick";
/** The time between the end of one round of the tick and the start of the next. */
export const ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS = ALERT_RULES.tickSeconds * 1000;
/**
 * The alert tick's mail leg, a job of its own (3f's review, operations2): its lock is `job:alert-mail`, and a round comes
 * ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS after the last one ended. A relay that answers slowly or not at all then holds only the mail
 * leg: alert_steps() and the channel's check keep their own time, so the pushes they write (the 15-minute escalation,
 * the deadline's reminders) are never late behind a mail.
 */
export const ALERT_MAIL_JOB = "alert-mail";

/**
 * The kinds whose mail is their push's sentence that the tick mails from a row, each a template of the mailer: every
 * kind of the contracts' SENTENCE_MAIL_KINDS, which a test holds this list to (3f's review, operations4: Task 5's two
 * kinds were pushed and never mailed).
 */
export const TICK_MAILED_KINDS: readonly StaffAlertKind[] = [
  "contact_mail",
  "contact_mail_escalated",
  "order_due",
  "mailbox_unreachable",
  "alert_channel_down",
  "order_opened",
  "order_corrected",
  "order_unverified",
  // Task 3.
  "order_effected",
  "order_reinstated",
  "hold_ending",
  // Task 6: copy_overdue, which alert_steps() writes daily, and copy_taken, which staffAlert writes after a download.
  "copy_overdue",
  "copy_taken",
  // Task 5's two daily kinds, joined in 3f's review: a report to an authority owed, and a hand-over's copy not destroyed.
  "report_owed",
  "handover_undestroyed",
  // 3d Task 1: quarantine_due, which alert_steps() writes daily, and quarantine_lost, which quarantine-record writes.
  "quarantine_due",
  "quarantine_lost",
  // 3d Task 2: release_undestroyed, which alert_steps() writes daily, and seal_released, which staffAlert writes after a release.
  "release_undestroyed",
  "seal_released",
];

/** A list of the contracts' words as a PostgreSQL array, for `= any(...)`: no word holds a comma or a quote. */
const words = (values: readonly string[]) => sql`${`{${values.join(",")}}`}::text[]`;

/**
 * The facts of an alert's push: the counts and times its kind names in ALERT_KINDS, never a handle, a lane's list or a
 * reason. 3c's and 3e's kinds keep their full message for the mail; the push gets these alone. A 3f alert's message is
 * its facts.
 */
export function alertFacts(message: StaffMessage): AlertFacts {
  switch (message.template) {
    case "moderation_urgent":
      return { count: message.count, oldestAt: message.oldest.toISOString() };
    case "moderation_waiting":
      // What the mail lists, each line's own count: the cases of each lane past its time, the cases that hold a measure
      // taken while deciding, and the replies waiting.
      return { count: message.lanes.reduce((sum, lane) => sum + Math.max(0, lane.count), 0) + message.interim + (message.replies?.count ?? 0) };
    case "moderation_burst":
      return { count: message.count };
    case "moderation_reads":
      return { limit: message.limit };
    case "moderation_reveal":
    case "moderation_csam_lifted":
      return { at: message.at.toISOString() };
    default:
      return message.facts;
  }
}

/** Writes one alert's row, with its kind's priority and scope; the database forces its times and its two legs as owed. */
async function insertAlert(q: Pick<ModerationDeps["apiDb"], "execute">, kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts): Promise<number> {
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  const [row] = await q.execute<{ id: string }>(
    sql`insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts) values (${kind}, ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${JSON.stringify(facts)}::jsonb) returning id`,
  );
  return Number(row!.id);
}

/**
 * Mails a 3f alert's row once: the row is taken FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED while its mail goes, and marked mailed when an
 * address took it, so staffAlert and the tick never both mail it. Answers how many addresses took it, or "elsewhere" when
 * another holds the row or it was mailed meanwhile.
 */
async function mailClaimed(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth">, id: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<number | "elsewhere"> {
  return deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    const claimed = await tx.execute(sql`select id from public.alert_outbox where id = ${id} and mailed_at is null for update skip locked`);
    if (claimed.length === 0) return "elsewhere";
    const accepted = await deps.auth.mailStaff(message);
    if (accepted > 0) await tx.execute(sql`update public.alert_outbox set mailed_at = now() where id = ${id}`);
    return accepted;
  });
}

/**
 * Sends a staff alert at most once in its key's window (null: no throttle, for a reveal and for a decision that lifted
 * the protection of reported images). After the throttle, in this order: it writes the alert's row of alert_outbox, which
 * the watcher pushes; then it mails every staff account. For 3c's and 3e's kinds (`mail: "own"`) the mail is the caller's
 * full message, and the row is marked mailed whether or not an address took it: the tick never renders such a mail from
 * a row. For a kind of 3f whose mail is its sentence, the row is marked only when an address took the mail, and the tick
 * mails a row left without it.
 *
 * An alert fails open: a row that cannot be written is logged and the mail goes all the same, and when the store cannot
 * be reached both go without a throttle. It answers sent when either leg took the alert. The hit is given back, so the
 * next occasion that meets the alert's condition sends it again, when the mail of one of 3c's and 3e's kinds went to
 * nobody (no row can mail it later), and for a kind of 3f only when neither leg took it. A failed give-back is logged.
 * It never throws for a failed send, which mailStaff logs.
 */
export async function staffAlert(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log">, key: string | null, windowMs: number, message: StaffMessage): Promise<"sent" | "throttled" | "unsent"> {
  let counted = false;
  if (key !== null) {
    try {
      const hit = await deps.limits.hit(key, windowMs);
      counted = true;
      if (hit.count > 1) return "throttled";
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key }, "moderation alert: the limit store could not be reached; the alert goes without its throttle");
    }
  }
  const kind = message.template;
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  let rowId: number | null = null;
  try {
    // A statement of its own, in a savepoint where the caller holds a transaction: a refused row never aborts it.
    rowId = await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => insertAlert(tx, kind, alertFacts(message)));
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key ?? kind }, "moderation alert: its row for the phones could not be written; the mail goes all the same");
  }
  let accepted: number;
  if (entry.mail === "sentence" && rowId !== null) {
    const mailed = await mailClaimed(deps, rowId, message).catch((err: unknown) => {
      deps.log.warn({ err, alert: rowId }, "moderation alert: its mail could not be sent now; the alert tick sends it");
      return 0;
    });
    accepted = mailed === "elsewhere" ? 1 : mailed;
  } else {
    accepted = await deps.auth.mailStaff(message);
    if (rowId !== null && entry.mail === "own") {
      await deps.apiDb
        .execute(sql`update public.alert_outbox set mailed_at = now() where id = ${rowId}`)
        .catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err, alert: rowId }, "moderation alert: its row could not be marked mailed; nothing mails it again"));
    }
  }
  const pushed = rowId !== null && entry.legs.includes("push");
  const giveBack = accepted === 0 && (entry.mail === "own" || !pushed);
  if (giveBack && counted && key !== null) {
    await deps.limits.release(key).catch((err: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err, alert: key }, "moderation alert: the hit of an alert nobody received could not be given back"));
  }
  return accepted > 0 || pushed ? "sent" : "unsent";
}

/**
 * The urgent lane's alert: when an intake has put an item into lane 0, every staff account is told how many cases wait
 * there and since when the oldest does, and the phone on call is woken. A notice about a post that quotes another puts
 * two cases into the lane and sends one alert that counts both. Best effort, after the commit and the answer; the
 * dispatch job repeats it while a lane-0 item still calls for someone.
 */
export async function alertUrgentLane(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log" | "config">): Promise<"sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "nothing_waiting"> {
  const waiting = await urgentWaiting(deps.apiDb);
  // Decided in the moment between the intake's commit and this read: nothing is left to alert about.
  if (waiting.count === 0 || waiting.oldest === null) return "nothing_waiting";
  // 3f's review (people4): the mail says whether the phone on call got the push, or that it is the only alert.
  return staffAlert(deps, URGENT_ALERT_KEY, URGENT_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, { template: "moderation_urgent", count: waiting.count, oldest: waiting.oldest, phones: deps.config.NOTIFY !== "off" });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the channel's health

/** The alert channel's state as the console's home and the tick read it, with the time since when. */
export interface ChannelHealth {
  channel: AlertChannelState;
  since: Date | null;
}

/**
 * The channel's state, read fresh (3f design, sections 5 and 7.2 step 3), by the database's clock: `off` with NOTIFY=off;
 * `down` while the watcher's beat is older than channel_down_minutes (or there never was one), or a row still owed its
 * push (a kind with a push leg, not pushed, younger than push_owed_minutes) is older than that while no publish has
 * worked for as long (push_ok_at; 3f's review, operations3: rows waiting behind ntfy's request limit, which answers and
 * takes some every round, never read as down, and Home never says that alerts arrive by mail only then); `mailbox`
 * while the beat is fresh and the mailbox was last read longer ago than that; `ok` otherwise. A row past its push's
 * bound counts for nothing any more, so the state clears by itself once the push server is back. `since` is the earliest
 * late time, or the clock's when there is none (a watcher that never beat, a mailbox never read).
 */
export async function channelHealth(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config">): Promise<ChannelHealth> {
  if (deps.config.NOTIFY === "off") return { channel: "off", since: null };
  const [row] = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ now: string; beat_at: string | null; mailbox_ok_at: string | null; owed_since: string | null; beat_late: boolean; owed_late: boolean; mailbox_late: boolean }>(sql`
    select now() as now, s.beat_at, s.mailbox_ok_at, o.owed_since,
           (s.beat_at is null or s.beat_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as beat_late,
           coalesce(o.owed_since < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes), false)
             and (s.push_ok_at is null or s.push_ok_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as owed_late,
           (s.mailbox_ok_at is null or s.mailbox_ok_at < now() - make_interval(mins => r.channel_down_minutes)) as mailbox_late
      from public.order_rules() r
      left join public.notify_state s on s.id = 1
      cross join lateral (select min(x.created_at) as owed_since from public.alert_outbox x
                           where x.pushed_at is null and x.kind = any(${words(PUSH_KINDS)})
                             and x.created_at > now() - make_interval(mins => r.push_owed_minutes)) o`);
  const at = (value: string | null) => (value === null ? null : new Date(value));
  const now = new Date(row!.now);
  if (row!.beat_late || row!.owed_late) {
    const late = [row!.beat_late ? at(row!.beat_at) : null, row!.owed_late ? at(row!.owed_since) : null].filter((d): d is Date => d !== null);
    return { channel: "down", since: late.length === 0 ? now : new Date(Math.min(...late.map((d) => d.getTime()))) };
  }
  if (row!.mailbox_late) return { channel: "mailbox", since: at(row!.mailbox_ok_at) ?? now };
  return { channel: "ok", since: null };
}

/**
 * The tick's own alarm: one row of `alert_channel_down` (mailed only) or `mailbox_unreachable` (pushed and mailed), at
 * most once in 24 hours by the outbox's own rows, with no key in the limit store. Answers whether it wrote one.
 */
async function raiseAlarm(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, kind: "alert_channel_down" | "mailbox_unreachable", since: Date): Promise<boolean> {
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
  const facts = JSON.stringify({ since: since.toISOString() });
  const rows = await deps.apiDb.execute(sql`
    insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts)
    select ${kind}, ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${facts}::jsonb
     where not exists (select 1 from public.alert_outbox o where o.kind = ${kind} and o.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => 24))
    returning id`);
  return rows.length > 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the alert tick

export interface TickReport {
  /** How many rows alert_steps() wrote, or null when the step failed. */
  steps: number | null;
  /** The channel's state, or null when NOTIFY is off or the step failed. */
  channel: AlertChannelState | null;
  /** The alarms the round raised. */
  raised: ("alert_channel_down" | "mailbox_unreachable")[];
}

/**
 * One round of the alert tick (3f design, section 7.2), each step in a try of its own:
 *   1. `select alert_steps()`: the database writes every time-driven row that is due;
 *   2. the channel's health, skipped with NOTIFY=off: its alarm rows, which the mail leg mails.
 * The mail leg (section 7.2's step 2) is alertMailLeg, a job of its own since 3f's review (ALERT_MAIL_JOB).
 */
export async function alertTick(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config" | "log">): Promise<TickReport> {
  const report: TickReport = { steps: null, channel: null, raised: [] };
  const step = async (name: string, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_TICK_JOB, step: name }, "alert-tick: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };

  await step("steps", async () => {
    const [row] = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ written: number }>(sql`select public.alert_steps() as written`);
    report.steps = Number(row!.written);
  });

  if (deps.config.NOTIFY === "on") {
    await step("channel", async () => {
      const health = await channelHealth(deps);
      report.channel = health.channel;
      if (health.channel === "down" && (await raiseAlarm(deps, "alert_channel_down", health.since!))) report.raised.push("alert_channel_down");
      if (health.channel === "mailbox" && (await raiseAlarm(deps, "mailbox_unreachable", health.since!))) report.raised.push("mailbox_unreachable");
    });
  }
  return report;
}

/**
 * One round of the mail leg (3f design, section 7.2 step 2): every row of a kind whose mail is its sentence, not yet
 * mailed and younger than ALERT_RULES.mailRetryHours, whoever wrote it, mailed to every staff account and marked when an
 * address took it; a row nobody took is tried again next round, and then left. Each row in a try of its own. It never
 * mails a row of 3c's or 3e's kinds: their mails say more than the row's facts, and staffAlert sends them. Answers how
 * many rows it mailed.
 */
export async function alertMailLeg(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "log">): Promise<number> {
  let mailedRows = 0;
  try {
    const rows = await deps.apiDb.execute<{ id: string; kind: StaffAlertKind; facts: AlertFacts }>(sql`
      select id, kind, facts from public.alert_outbox
       where mailed_at is null and kind = any(${words(TICK_MAILED_KINDS)})
         and created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => ${ALERT_RULES.mailRetryHours})
       order by id`);
    for (const row of rows) {
      try {
        const mailed = await mailClaimed(deps, Number(row.id), { template: row.kind, facts: row.facts });
        if (typeof mailed === "number" && mailed > 0) mailedRows++;
        else if (mailed === 0) deps.log.warn({ job: ALERT_MAIL_JOB, alert: row.id, kind: row.kind }, "alert-mail: no staff address took an alert's mail; it is tried again next round");
      } catch (err) {
        deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_MAIL_JOB, alert: row.id }, "alert-mail: an alert's mail failed; it is tried again next round");
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, job: ALERT_MAIL_JOB }, "alert-mail: the rows owed their mail could not be read; the next round reads them again");
  }
  return mailedRows;
}

/** The alert tick as a job of the shared lock: a round ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS after the last one ended, on one instance at a time. */
export function createAlertTick(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: ALERT_TICK_JOB, intervalMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => alertTick(deps) });
}

/** The mail leg as a job of the shared lock under a key of its own, at the tick's interval, so a slow relay holds only it. */
export function createAlertMailJob(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: ALERT_MAIL_JOB, intervalMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: ALERT_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => alertMailLeg(deps) });
}
```

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE, AppealsReviewedParams, DAILY_LIMITS, type AppealRequest, type AppealRow, type AppealsPage, type DecisionView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { REDRESS_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import { isDeadlock, isLockNotAvailable } from "../lib/lock-bounds";
import { authorDecisionView, decodeListCursor, encodeListCursor } from "./author";
import { reviewerOf } from "./cases";
import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { recordConfirmed, refuseUnopened, subjectLockMode, type AnsweredFacts, type DecideContext, type DecideOptions, type DecideOutcome } from "./decide";
import { countOrRefuse, saltedStatement } from "./intake";
import { releasedSeals } from "./release";
import { holdsAnnouncedStanding, insertAction, insertAppeal, insertReview, pendingAppeals, raisedMessage, reviewedDecision, violatedUniqueConstraint } from "./repo";

/**
 * Appeals and their reviews (3c design, sections 6.3 and 7.7). An appeal has one shape: the author's appeal of a final
 * decision that restricts them, one for each such decision, while any of its measures is in force and within six
 * calendar months of being told. A review answers that one appeal: it keeps the decision or lifts measures of it, and
 * never restricts. The database decides whether an appeal is open and who may review it; this file inserts the rows.
 */

const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;

/**
 * The longest an appeal waits for a lock. Its trigger takes the case's row for the length of its own transaction and
 * waits for whoever holds the case: a decision that is being recorded, which for a seal over thousands of images is
 * seconds, or an erasure.
 */
const APPEAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** How often the appeal's transaction is run again after a deadlock or a lock timeout: in each nothing was written. */
const APPEAL_RETRIES = 2;

/**
 * POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/appeal: the author's appeal of a decision about their post or their account. In
 * this order:
 *   1. the day's limit, five for an account, counted before anything is read, so that whatever the answer the request
 *      was counted;
 *   2. one transaction that inserts the appeal's row. Its trigger decides, under a lock on the decision's case, whether
 *      an appeal of this decision is open now for this account (appeal_not_open: the decision is not a final
 *      restriction, is someone else's, is past its window, or nothing of it is in force), and the unique index refuses
 *      a second appeal (appeal_exists). The statement is optional and free of form; the server makes its salt and
 *      digest. A deadlock or a lock timeout runs the transaction again, and when the last run fails the same way the
 *      answer is service_unavailable;
 *   3. the answer: the decision as its author now reads it, with the appeal waiting. A decision that is not the
 *      viewer's, or of which they were not told, never opened by its id and does not now: not_found.
 * A request that failed through no fault of its sender gives its hit on the day's limit back.
 */
export async function fileAppeal(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "limits" | "log">, viewer: string, decisionId: string, request: AppealRequest): Promise<DecisionView> {
  const key = `appeal:day:account:${viewer}`;
  await countOrRefuse(deps, key, DAY_MS, DAILY_LIMITS.appeals);
  const statement = await saltedStatement(request.statement);
  try {
    for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
      try {
        await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
          await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${APPEAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
          await insertAppeal(tx, { decisionId, appellantId: viewer, statement });
        });
        break;
      } catch (err) {
        const refusal = raisedMessage(err);
        if (refusal !== null && isModerationErrorCode(refusal)) throw new ModerationError(refusal);
        if (violatedUniqueConstraint(err) === "appeals_once") throw new ModerationError("appeal_exists");
        if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
        if (attempt >= APPEAL_RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("service_unavailable", 503, undefined, 30);
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    // A refusal that is the sender's own (not open, appealed already) stays counted; anything else was not their doing.
    if (!(err instanceof ModerationError) || err.code === "service_unavailable") {
      await deps.limits.release(key).catch((failure: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err: failure }, "appeal: a limit hit of a request that could not be saved could not be given back"));
    }
    throw err;
  }
  return authorDecisionView(deps, viewer, decisionId);
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/appeals: the pending appeals, 50 a page, each marked whether the reading person may review it (3c
 * design, section 7.7). No row carries a statement: the reviewer reads it on the case page, whose read is logged and
 * counted. 3e (section 7.11 item 6): the first page lists first the appeals of a decision that holds a running suspension
 * or a termination that stands, oldest first, since the person can do nothing while they wait; then the rest, newest
 * first, which the cursor pages through. The first group is read on the first page alone, up to a page of it: as many
 * appeals of running measures as a page holds are far more than one or two staff accounts can have waiting.
 */
export async function appealsList(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, cursor?: string): Promise<AppealsPage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeListCursor(cursor);
  const first = after === null ? await pendingAppeals(deps.apiDb, reviewerOf(session), null, APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE, true) : [];
  const room = APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE - first.length;
  const rest = room > 0 ? await pendingAppeals(deps.apiDb, reviewerOf(session), after, room + 1) : [];
  const page = [...first, ...rest.slice(0, room)];
  // The cursor is the last row of the rest: the first group is never paged.
  const last = rest.slice(0, room).at(-1);
  // 3d Task 2 (sections 7.2 and 8.7): an appeal of a seal whose posts were released stays open, marked with the release.
  const released = await releasedSeals(deps.apiDb, page.map((row) => row.decisionId));
  return {
    appeals: page.map(
      (row): AppealRow => ({
        id: row.id,
        caseId: row.caseId,
        decisionId: row.decisionId,
        filedAt: row.filedAt,
        decidedAt: row.decidedAt,
        deadline: row.deadline,
        ruleId: row.ruleId as AppealRow["ruleId"],
        legal: row.legal,
        actions: row.actions,
        reviewer: row.reviewer,
        needsAdmin: row.needsAdmin,
        mayReview: row.mayReview,
        standingFirst: row.standingFirst,
        // Only a released seal adds the mark; a row of any other appeal stays as it was.
        ...(released.has(row.decisionId) ? { released: released.get(row.decisionId)! } : {}),
      }),
    ),
    // One row more than the room was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: rest.length > room && last ? encodeListCursor({ at: last.sortAt, id: last.id }) : null,
  };
}

/**
 * POST /api/staff/decisions/:decision/review, once its step-up verified (3c design, section 7.7): records the answer to
 * the author's one appeal of the decision, as a decision of kind review, in the one transaction every confirmed decision
 * runs (recordConfirmed), with its audit row as appeals_reviewed on the reviewed decision.
 *
 * Before the transaction: the redress texts are those the API serves now (the rulebook version is the reviewed
 * decision's, which the database holds the review to), and the appeal the reviewer's key confirmed is the decision's
 * pending appeal: when it is not, the appeal was answered since the console read the case, and the answer is
 * case_changed with nothing written. The database forces and compares the appeal again under the case's lock, and at
 * commit holds the audit row's params to the stored review, so a review answers exactly the appeal that was confirmed.
 * It refuses a reviewer who decided anything in the case or opened a finding in it (reviewer_conflict), a party
 * (staff_recused), and a moderator where the review needs an admin (admin_required).
 *
 * After the commit the transaction's own last step does what it does for every decision: the statement's mail, the
 * count of the person's decisions, and the mail to every staff account when the review lifted a seal.
 */
export async function review(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: DecideContext, options: DecideOptions = {}): Promise<DecideOutcome> {
  // A confirmation of anything else never reviews an appeal: that would be a wiring fault, not a refusal.
  if (confirmed.action !== "appeals_reviewed" || confirmed.target.type !== "decision" || confirmed.keyId !== session.keyId) {
    throw new Error("a review needs a step-up that confirmed it");
  }
  const params = AppealsReviewedParams.parse(confirmed.params);
  if (params.redressVersion !== REDRESS_VERSION) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
  // The routes' one list of the kinds they accept (3e design, section 7.1 item 2).
  refuseUnopened(params, options);

  const reviewsDecisionId = confirmed.target.id;
  const reviewed = await reviewedDecision(deps.apiDb, reviewsDecisionId);
  if (!reviewed) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  if (reviewed.pendingAppealId !== params.appealId) throw new ModerationError("case_changed");
  // As for a decision: a case's target and a post's author never change, so the subject is read before the transaction.
  const subject = reviewed.target.type === "account" ? reviewed.target.id : await deps.social.postAuthor(reviewed.target.id);

  // A review holds reversals only, so its first lock stays FOR NO KEY UPDATE (3e design, section 5), a lift included,
  // but for one that keeps an announced suspension or termination in force, and so may fix its start (Task 4).
  const answered: AnsweredFacts = { kind: "review", outcome: params.outcome, holdsAnnounced: await holdsAnnouncedStanding(deps.apiDb, reviewsDecisionId) };
  return recordConfirmed(
    deps,
    session,
    confirmed,
    ctx,
    subject,
    async (tx, decisionId) => {
      await insertReview(tx, { id: decisionId, caseId: reviewed.caseId, reviewsDecisionId, decidedBy: session.userId, params });
      for (const action of params.actions) await insertAction(tx, decisionId, action);
    },
    subjectLockMode(params.actions, answered),
    reviewed.target,
  );
}

/** The case a reviewed decision belongs to, for the answer to a review that has just committed. */
export async function reviewedCase(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, decisionId: string): Promise<string> {
  const reviewed = await reviewedDecision(deps.apiDb, decisionId);
  if (!reviewed) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  return reviewed.caseId;
}
```

```ts
import { authorStanding, caseStanding, strikeDue } from "./standing";
import { caseReplies, repliesWaiting, standingColumns, standingOnDecisions, strikeAccounts, unansweredReplies, type ReplyColumns } from "./standing-repo";

import {
```
