} from "./repo";

/** A reply as the case page shows it: its text while korbat keeps it, which an erasure blanks. */
const replyOf = (reply: ReplyColumns | undefined): CaseDecisionAction["reply"] =>
  reply === undefined ? null : { filedAt: reply.filedAt, onTime: reply.onTime, text: reply.erasedAt === null ? reply.text : null, answeredAt: reply.answeredAt, answeredBy: reply.answeredBy };

/**
 * The queue and the case, for staff (3c design, section 7.3): the overview the home screen shows, the queue, the case
 * answer, the one door to a case's images, a fresh snapshot, and a moderator's own finding. Every read of a case is
 * written to the access log and counts against the day's limit; none of it needs the key.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the day, and the bands of a reporter's summary

/** How many seconds are left to midnight UTC, at least one: what a refusal at a daily limit tells the console to wait. */
export function secondsToUtcMidnight(now: Date): number {
  const midnight = Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate() + 1);
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil((midnight - now.getTime()) / 1000));
}

/** The same moment `months` calendar months later in UTC; a day the target month lacks becomes that month's last day. */
function monthsAfter(at: Date, months: number): Date {
  const month = at.getUTCMonth() + months;
  const lastDay = new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month, Math.min(at.getUTCDate(), lastDay), at.getUTCHours(), at.getUTCMinutes(), at.getUTCSeconds(), at.getUTCMilliseconds()));
}

/** A reporter's account age as a band: under one month, one to twelve months (both ends included), or over twelve. */
export function accountAgeBand(createdAt: Date, now: Date): NonNullable<SourceSummary["accountAge"]> {
  if (now.getTime() < monthsAfter(createdAt, 1).getTime()) return "under_1_month";
  return now.getTime() <= monthsAfter(createdAt, 12).getTime() ? "1_to_12_months" : "over_12_months";
}

/** How many items a reporter filed, the one being read included, as a band. */
export function itemsFiledBand(filed: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["itemsFiled"]> {
  if (filed <= 1) return "1";
  return filed <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/** The share of a reporter's decided items that were acted on, as a band; exactly half is "half or more". */
export function actedOnBand(decided: number, actedOn: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["actedOn"]> {
  if (decided <= 0) return "none_decided";
  if (actedOn <= 0) return "none";
  return actedOn * 2 < decided ? "under_half" : "half_or_more";
}

/** How many of a reporter's items were answered while nobody could open the images, as a band; they are counted apart from the decided ones. */
export function answeredUnseenBand(unseen: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["answeredUnseen"]> {
  if (unseen <= 0) return "none";
  if (unseen === 1) return "1";
  return unseen <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/**
 * Each reporter's place among the reporters of one case, from 0, in the order of each one's first item in the case: the
 * letter the case page gives them. Given per case, so one person's letter on one case says nothing about another.
 */
export function reporterIndexes(reportersInItemOrder: readonly (string | null)[]): Map<string, number> {
  const indexes = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const reporter of reportersInItemOrder) if (reporter !== null && !indexes.has(reporter)) indexes.set(reporter, indexes.size);
  return indexes;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- recusal

/**
 * Refuses a staff account that is too close to the case's subject: every route that names a case, or an item of one,
 * asks this first, so a refused read writes no access row and does not count against the day's limit. The check never
 * looks at who reported, and its answer reads the same whoever the conflict concerns.
 */
export async function refuseRecused(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<void> {
  if (await staffCaseConflict(deps.apiDb, session.userId, caseId)) throw new ModerationError("staff_recused");
}

/** The case, after the recusal check; not_found when no case has the id. */
async function openableCase(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseRow> {
  await refuseRecused(deps, session, caseId);
  const row = await caseById(deps.apiDb, caseId);
  if (!row) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  return row;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the overview

/** The reading person as the review marks ask about them: the session's account, and whether its role is admin. */
export const reviewerOf = (session: ActiveStaffSession) => ({ id: session.userId, admin: session.role === "admin" });

/** How long the overview's late erasures are kept before they are read again. */
export const ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS = 60_000;

/** The late erasures last read on a pool, and when: one read serves every staff member's home screen for a minute. */
const lateByPool = new WeakMap<object, { at: number; counts: Promise<ErasureOverdue> }>();

/**
 * The overview's erasureOverdue (3c design, section 7.3): one count for each due rule of what a step of the retention
 * job or the auth janitor should have changed more than a day ago and has not. The image rows are the media module's to
 * count and the notifiers' contacts the auth module's, since this module names neither.
 *
 * The counts are read at most once a minute for all staff, and a read in flight is shared: the count of late image rows
 * reads the freeze once for each kept row of a frozen account's deleted posts (seconds at twenty thousand rows), which a
 * home screen must not pay on every load, and both jobs run only every ten minutes, so a count a minute old says the
 * same. A read that failed is not kept.
 */
export function erasureOverdue(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "auth" | "now">): Promise<ErasureOverdue> {
  const now = deps.now().getTime();
  const kept = lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb);
  if (kept && now >= kept.at && now - kept.at < ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS) return kept.counts;
  const counts = (async (): Promise<ErasureOverdue> => {
    const late = await lateErasures(deps.apiDb, RETENTION);
    return { ...late, images: await deps.media.overdueDeletions(), contacts: await deps.auth.overdueContacts() };
  })();
  lateByPool.set(deps.apiDb, { at: now, counts });
  counts.catch(() => {
    if (lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb)?.counts === counts) lateByPool.delete(deps.apiDb);
  });
  return counts;
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/overview: counts, times, staff handles and cases, for every staff member's home screen. One number is
 * the reading person's own: how many of the waiting appeals they may review.
 */
export async function overview(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config" | "media" | "auth" | "now">, session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffOverview> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const byLane = await openByLane(q);
  const today = await staffToday(q);
  const mails = await mailAndReleaseCounts(q, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
  const appeals = await appealCounts(q, reviewerOf(session));
  return {
    lanes: ([0, 1, 2] as const).map((lane) => byLane.find((row) => row.lane === lane) ?? { lane, open: 0, oldestAt: null }),
    appealsWaiting: appeals.waiting,
    appealsYouMayReview: appeals.mayReview,
    appealsWithoutReviewer: appeals.withoutReviewer,
    reveals: await recentReveals(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    imagesToday: today.images,
    findingsToday: today.findings,
    mailsWaiting: mails.waiting,
    mailsFailed: mails.failed,
    releaseOverdue: mails.releaseOverdue,
    erasureOverdue: await erasureOverdue(deps),
    deferUnproven: deps.config.MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN === "on",
    // The three lists of the path for child sexual abuse material, which every staff member sees: what lifted the
    // protection of reported images, who chose not to seal, and which seals taken while deciding stand.
    protectionLifted: await recentProtectionLifted(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    sealsDeclined: await recentSealsDeclined(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    interimSeals: await interimSealsInForce(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    // 3e (design, section 8.8): the replies no decision answered, and the accounts at the ladder's number of strikes.
    repliesWaiting: await repliesWaiting(q),
    strikeAccounts: (await strikeAccounts(q, 1)).total,
    // 3f (design, sections 8.2 and 10.2): the contact point's messages nobody has handled, and the alert channel's state,
    // both read fresh.
    contact: await contactOverview(deps),
    alerts: await channelAlerts(deps),
    // Task 3: the orders given effect and not verified, or holding a disabled post added after their check.
    ordersUnverified: await unverifiedOrders(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    // Task 5: the reports to the authorities owed, from reports_owed() and nothing more: a case, a kind, a time.
    reportsOwed: await reportsOwed(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    // Task 6: the copy's age, by alert_steps()'s own rule for copy_overdue; and after a restore the open gaps, the measures
    // among them and the newest import's time.
    copy: await copyOverview(q),
    restore: await restoreOverview(q),
    // 3d Task 1 (sections 7.1 and 8.2): the moves into and out of the quarantine that are due, and the files to destroy,
    // from quarantine_counts() alone.
    quarantine: await quarantineCounts(q),
    // 3d Task 2 (sections 7.2 and 8.2): the acts of the last 30 days that cannot be taken back, as 3c lists a lifted seal:
    // the releases of sealed images, each with its seal's case ([home.released]).
    destructive: await recentReleases(q, DESTRUCTIVE_DAYS, DESTRUCTIVE_MAX),
  };
}

/** 3d Task 2: each appeal of the case whose decision's seal released posts marked with that release; any other appeal stays as it was. */
async function withReleases<T extends { decisionId: string }>(q: Parameters<typeof releasedSeals>[0], appeals: T[]): Promise<(T & { released?: { at: string; basis: "leave" | "period" } })[]> {
  const released = await releasedSeals(q, appeals.map((appeal) => appeal.decisionId));
  return appeals.map((appeal) => (released.has(appeal.decisionId) ? { ...appeal, released: released.get(appeal.decisionId)! } : appeal));
}

/** StaffOverview.alerts: the channel's state as the tick judges it, with the time since when. */
async function channelAlerts(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config">): Promise<StaffOverview["alerts"]> {
  const health = await channelHealth(deps);
  return { channel: health.channel, since: health.since?.toISOString() ?? null };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the queue

const CURSOR_TIME = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}[.][0-9]{6}Z$/;
const CURSOR_ID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

/** The queue's cursor: the last row's sort key as an opaque word. */
const encodeCursor = (row: QueueCursor): string => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify([row.lane, row.deferred, row.sortAt, row.id]), "utf8").toString("base64url");

/** Reads a cursor back; anything this module did not write is refused, never guessed at. */
function decodeCursor(cursor: string): QueueCursor {
  let parts: unknown;
  try {
    parts = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cursor, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(parts) || parts.length !== 4) throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  const [lane, deferred, sortAt, id] = parts as unknown[];
  if ((lane !== 0 && lane !== 1 && lane !== 2) || typeof deferred !== "boolean" || typeof sortAt !== "string" || !CURSOR_TIME.test(sortAt) || typeof id !== "string" || !CURSOR_ID.test(id)) {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  return { lane, deferred, sortAt, id };
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/queue: open cases by lane and age, 50 a page. Only under the emergency switch are cases whose unanswered
 * items all come from unproven sources sorted after the others of their lane, never below a less severe lane.
 */
export async function queue(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config">, cursor?: string): Promise<QueuePage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeCursor(cursor);
  const found = await queueRows(deps.apiDb, { deferUnproven: deps.config.MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN === "on", after, limit: QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE + 1 });
  const page = found.slice(0, QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE);
  const last = page.at(-1);
  return {
    cases: page.map(
      (row): QueueRow => ({
        id: row.id,
        lane: row.lane,
        targetType: row.targetType,
        openedAt: row.openedAt,
        oldestOpenAt: row.oldestOpenAt,
        openItems: row.openItems,
        rules: row.rules as QueueRow["rules"],
        categories: row.categories as QueueRow["categories"],
        allegesIllegal: row.allegesIllegal,
        suspect: row.suspect,
        reexamination: row.reexamination,
        deferred: row.deferred,
      }),
    ),
    // One row more than the page was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: found.length > QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE && last ? encodeCursor(last) : null,
    // 3e (design, section 8.5): the first page leads with the replies no decision answered, oldest first, without text.
    replies: after === null ? await unansweredReplies(deps.apiDb, QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE) : [],
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the case answer

/** A snapshot as the case answer carries it: its content unless the database's one predicate withholds it. */
function snapshotView(snapshot: SnapshotRead): CaseSnapshot {
  if (snapshot.withheld || snapshot.salt === null) return { id: snapshot.id, takenAt: snapshot.takenAt, digest: snapshot.digest, withheld: true };
  return {
    id: snapshot.id,
    takenAt: snapshot.takenAt,
    digest: snapshot.digest,
    withheld: false,
    salt: snapshot.salt,
    targetType: snapshot.targetType,
    targetId: snapshot.targetId,
    authorHandle: snapshot.authorHandle,
    postState: snapshot.postState,
    postCreatedAt: snapshot.postCreatedAt,
    replyToId: snapshot.replyToId,
    quoteOfId: snapshot.quoteOfId,
    body: snapshot.body,
    media: snapshot.media,
    displayName: snapshot.displayName,
    bio: snapshot.bio,
    handle: snapshot.handle,
  };
}

const NO_BANDS = { accountAge: null, itemsFiled: null, actedOn: null, answeredUnseen: null } as const;
const NO_CONTACT = { named: null, contactGiven: null, confirmed: null, suppressed: null, contactLost: false } as const;

/**
 * Who sent an item, as a summary that names nobody (3c design, section 7.3). A finding was found by a moderator; a notice
 * on the path for child sexual abuse material is anonymous, whoever sent it; a signed-out notifier is what the auth
 * module says of the contact, never the contact; a signed-in reporter is a letter and four bands, or, once the link to
 * the account is gone, only that.
 */
function sourceOf(item: CaseItemRow, letters: Map<string, number>, reporters: Map<string, ReporterFacts>, contacts: Map<string, NotifierFacts>, now: Date): SourceSummary {
  if (item.intakeKind === "finding") return { kind: "staff", label: SOURCE_LABELS.staff, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  // 3f (design, section 8.6): an order's item names its authority's order, never a reporter.
  if (item.intakeKind === "order") return { kind: "authority", label: SOURCE_LABELS.authority, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  if (item.csam) return { kind: "anonymous", label: SOURCE_LABELS.anonymous, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  if (item.channel === "signed_out") {
    const facts = item.contactId === null ? undefined : contacts.get(item.contactId);
    return {
      kind: "notifier",
      label: SOURCE_LABELS.notifier,
      ...NO_BANDS,
      named: facts?.named ?? false,
      contactGiven: facts?.contactGiven ?? false,
      confirmed: facts?.confirmed ?? false,
      suppressed: facts?.suppressed ?? false,
      // The notice left a contact that the auth module no longer has: never stored, or forgotten since.
      contactLost: item.contactId !== null && !(facts?.found ?? false),
    };
  }
  if (item.reporterAccountId === null) return { kind: "unlinked", label: SOURCE_LABELS.unlinked, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  const facts = reporters.get(item.reporterAccountId);
  return {
    kind: "reporter",
    label: reporterLabel(letters.get(item.reporterAccountId) ?? 0),
    accountAge: facts?.createdAt ? accountAgeBand(facts.createdAt, now) : null,
    itemsFiled: itemsFiledBand(facts?.filed ?? 1),
    actedOn: actedOnBand(facts?.decided ?? 0, facts?.actedOn ?? 0),
    answeredUnseen: answeredUnseenBand(facts?.answeredUnseen ?? 0),
    ...NO_CONTACT,
  };
}

/** Whether an item's source is a signed-in reporter still linked to an account: the only items that get a letter. */
const linkedReporter = (item: CaseItemRow): string | null => (item.intakeKind === "user" && !item.csam && item.channel === "signed_in" ? item.reporterAccountId : null);

/**
 * The case as staff read it: what is, never what its senders are told (the status page keeps a live target from a dead
 * one; this answer does not). It writes nothing: readCase logs the read and holds it to the day's limit.
 */
export async function caseView(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "media" | "config" | "now">, session: ActiveStaffSession, row: CaseRow): Promise<CaseView> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const origin = deps.config.APP_ORIGIN;

  // The target as it stands. An account case shows no image: a profile holds none, and the images of its posts are shown
  // only on those posts' own cases.
  let target: CaseTarget;
  let imagesAllowed = false;
  let authorId: string | null;
  if (row.targetType === "post") {
    const post = await livePost(q, row.targetId);
    target = { type: "post", id: row.targetId, link: postLink(origin, row.targetId), authorHandle: post?.authorHandle ?? null, state: post?.state ?? null, level: post?.level ?? null };
    imagesAllowed = post?.imagesAllowed ?? false;
    authorId = post?.authorId ?? null;
  } else {
    const account = await liveAccount(q, row.targetId);
    target = { type: "account", id: row.targetId, handle: account?.handle ?? null, displayName: account?.displayName ?? null, bio: account?.bio ?? null, deleted: account?.deleted ?? false };
    authorId = row.targetId;
  }

  // What the page shows in place of images on the path for child sexual abuse material: counts and days only.
  const marks = await suspicionOf(q, row.id);
  let suspicion: CaseView["suspicion"] = null;
  if (marks.holds) {
    const reach = await deps.media.reach({ type: row.targetType, id: row.targetId });
    const earlier = await earlierAnswers(q, { type: row.targetType, id: row.targetId }, authorId, SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS);
    suspicion = {
      open: marks.open,
      reach: { posts: reach.posts, images: reach.images, sealed: reach.sealed, served: reach.served, newestPostOn: reach.newestPostOn },
      // Only a post's images are ever shown in the console, so only a post's case can say when staff last looked.
      earlier: { target: { ...earlier.target, imagesOpenedOn: row.targetType === "post" ? await imagesOpenedOn(q, row.targetId) : null }, author: earlier.author },
    };
  }

  const itemRows = await caseItems(q, row.id, session.userId);
  const letters = reporterIndexes(itemRows.map(linkedReporter));
  const reporters = await reporterFacts(q, [...letters.keys()]);
  const contactIds = [...new Set(itemRows.flatMap((item) => (item.channel === "signed_out" && !item.csam && item.contactId !== null ? [item.contactId] : [])))];
  const contacts = contactIds.length === 0 ? new Map<string, NotifierFacts>() : await deps.auth.notifierFacts(contactIds);
  const now = deps.now();
  const items = itemRows.map(
    (item): CaseItem => ({
      id: item.id,
      seq: item.seq,
      position: item.position,
      createdAt: item.createdAt,
      lane: item.lane,
      // An account's address is built from the handle as it was named; the target above carries the handle it holds now.
      link: item.targetType === "post" ? postLink(origin, item.targetId) : accountLink(origin, item.namedHandle ?? ""),
      ruleId: item.ruleId as CaseItem["ruleId"],
      allegesIllegal: item.allegesIllegal,
      csam: item.csam,
      category: item.category as CaseItem["category"],
      categoryKeyword: item.categoryKeyword,
      citedLaw: item.citedLaw,
      explanation: item.explanation,
      mediaId: item.mediaId,
      suspect: item.suspect,
      // An item korbat added for a quoted post stands ten positions after the item it was added for.
      quotedByPosition: item.position > 10 ? item.position - 10 : null,
      quotedCaseId: item.quotedCaseId,
      reexaminesPosition: item.reexaminesPosition,
      reexaminesYourDecision: item.reexaminesYourDecision,
      statement: item.statement,
      outcome: item.outcome as CaseItem["outcome"],
      answeredBy: item.answeredBy,
      erased: item.erased,
      source: sourceOf(item, letters, reporters, contacts, now),
      // 3e Task 5: the mark "manifestly unfounded": whether one may be set, and whether it stands or was withdrawn.
      markable: item.markable,
      unfounded: item.unfounded,
      markWithdrawn: item.markWithdrawn,
      orderId: item.orderId,
    }),
  );

  const actions = await caseActions(q, row.id);
  // The columns of 3e of every ledger row of the case, with a standing measure's period as it stands now.
  const columns = await standingColumns(q, row.id);
  // 3e Task 3: the standing measures that rest on each decision of the case, which a review or a correction would end.
  const standingOn = await standingOnDecisions(q, row.id);
  // 3e Task 4: the replies to the case's standing measures, with their texts: read here, in the logged read, and nowhere else.
  const replies = await caseReplies(q, row.id);
  // 3f Task 3: an order's measure names its order and whether it keeps the post from its author; a reinstatement its ground.
  const orderFacts = await caseOrderFacts(q, row.id);
  // 3d Task 1 (sections 6.1, 8.4 and 10.3): where the files of each seal for good of the case are, read for the seals of
  // the decisions that are not interim: a seal taken while deciding leaves its files in the store.
  const caseDecisionRows = await caseDecisions(q, row.id);
  const sealsForGood = actions.filter(
    (action) => action.kind === "seal_media" && caseDecisionRows.some((decision) => decision.id === action.decisionId && decision.kind !== "interim"),
  );
  const custody = await sealCustody(q, sealsForGood.map((action) => action.id));
  // 3d Task 2 (sections 7.2, 8.5 and 10.3): the release block of each seal for good that is in force, with the facts of
  // release_facts and the posts the next release would name; a seal that is lifted has none.
  const releases = await releaseBlocks(q, sealsForGood.filter((action) => action.inForce).map((action) => action.id));
  const custodyOf = (actionId: string | undefined) =>
    actionId === undefined ? {} : { ...(custody.has(actionId) ? { custody: custody.get(actionId)! } : {}), ...(releases.has(actionId) ? { release: releases.get(actionId)! } : {}) };
  const decisions: CaseDecision[] = [];
  for (const decision of caseDecisionRows) {
    const own: CaseDecision["actions"] = [];
    for (const action of actions.filter((candidate) => candidate.decisionId === decision.id)) {
      const more = columns.get(action.id);
      own.push({
        id: action.id,
        kind: action.kind,
        mediaId: action.mediaId,
        noEffect: action.noEffect,
        inForce: action.inForce,
        reversesActionId: action.reversesActionId,
        liftedBy: action.liftedBy,
        // A seal's list is the database's, written when the seal was recorded: text for the report to the police.
        sealed: action.kind === "seal_media" ? await sealCovers(q, action.id, SEAL_LIST_MAX) : null,
        days: more?.days ?? null,
        announced: more?.announced ?? null,
        basis: (more?.basis ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["basis"],
        restsOn: more?.restsOn ?? null,
        earliestStart: more?.earliestStart ?? null,
        countsUntil: more?.countsUntil ?? null,
        period: (more?.period ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["period"],
        restedOnBy: (more?.restedOnBy ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["restedOnBy"],
        // 3e Task 2: a retirement names the handle it retired; no other row carries the member.
        ...(more?.handle ? { handle: more.handle } : {}),
        reply: replyOf(replies.get(action.id)),
        ...(orderFacts.get(action.id) ?? {}),
      });
    }
    decisions.push({
      id: decision.id,
      kind: decision.kind,
      outcome: decision.outcome as CaseDecision["outcome"],
      ground: decision.ground as CaseDecision["ground"],
      ruleId: decision.ruleId as CaseDecision["ruleId"],
      rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
      redressVersion: decision.redressVersion,
      category: decision.category as CaseDecision["category"],
      categoryKeyword: decision.categoryKeyword,
      source: decision.source as CaseDecision["source"],
      decidedAt: decision.decidedAt,
      staffHandle: decision.staffHandle,
      throughSeq: decision.throughSeq,
      answersFromSeq: decision.answersFromSeq,
      reviewsDecisionId: decision.reviewsDecisionId,
      snapshotId: decision.snapshotId,
      suspect: decision.suspect,
      unseen: decision.unseen,
      needsAdmin: decision.needsAdmin,
      endedInterim: decision.endedInterim,
      facts: decision.facts,
      reason: decision.reason,
      legalReference: decision.legalReference,
      actions: own,
      ...(standingOn.has(decision.id) ? { standingOn: standingOn.get(decision.id)!.map((entry) => ({ kind: entry.kind, basis: entry.basis as StandingBasis })) } : {}),
      ...custodyOf(sealsForGood.find((action) => action.decisionId === decision.id)?.id),
    });
  }

  const texts = await caseStaffTexts(q, row.id);
  const staffText = (text: (typeof texts)[number]) => ({ id: text.id, staffHandle: text.staffHandle, createdAt: text.createdAt, text: text.text });
  return {
    id: row.id,
    lane: row.lane,
    stateVersion: row.stateVersion,
    intakeSeq: row.intakeSeq,
    answeredSeq: row.answeredSeq,
    openedAt: row.openedAt,
    closedAt: row.closedAt,
    target,
    suspicion,
    imagesAllowed,
    snapshots: (await caseSnapshots(q, row.id)).map(snapshotView),
    items,
    decisions,
    appeals: await withReleases(q, await caseAppeals(q, row.id, reviewerOf(session))),
    drafts: (await ownDrafts(q, row.id, session.userId)) as StaffTextDraft[],
    notes: texts.filter((text) => text.kind === "note").map(staffText),
    sealsDeclined: texts.filter((text) => text.kind === "seal_declined").map(staffText),
    history: (await caseHistory(q, row.id)) as CaseHistoryEntry[],
    // 3e: on a post case whether a final restriction gives a strike and its author's standing in bands (the author of a
    // post that is gone has none to show); on an account case the account's standing.
    strikeDue: row.targetType === "post" ? await strikeDue(q, row.id) : null,
    authorStanding: row.targetType === "post" && authorId !== null ? await authorStanding(q, authorId) : null,
    standing: row.targetType === "account" ? await caseStanding(q, row.id, row.targetId) : null,
    // 3f (sections 8.6 and 10.2): whether the post is preserved for an order, and whether an order's notice about it is held.
    preserved: row.targetType === "post" ? await postPreserved(q, row.targetId) : false,
    noticeHeld: row.targetType === "post" ? await noticeHeldOn(q, row.targetId) : null,
    // Task 4 (section 8.6, [reinstate.erased]): the day an order's preservation ended by erasing the post, if one did.
    orderErasedOn: row.targetType === "post" ? await orderErasedOn(q, row.targetId) : null,
    // Task 5 (sections 7.13 and 10.2): since when a report to the authorities is owed for this case, from reports_owed().
    reportOwed: await reportOwedOn(q, row.id),
  };
}

/** The alert's key for one staff account's day: its window ends at midnight UTC, so the alert goes once that day. */
const readsKey = (staffId: string) => `moderation-reads:${staffId}`;

/**
 * Tells every staff account, the person's own included, that a staff account reached the day's limit on cases: a stolen
 * key reads at the speed of requests, and this mail is how the others learn of it. Once a day for each account.
 */
async function alertDailyReads(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log" | "now">, staffId: string, limit: number): Promise<void> {
  const handle = (await handleOf(deps.apiDb, staffId)) ?? "unknown";
  await staffAlert(deps, readsKey(staffId), secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()) * 1000, { template: "moderation_reads", handle, limit });
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/cases/:case. In this order: the recusal check; the day's limit, which counts different cases, so a case
 * the person already opened today is never refused and a reload or a decision's answer never meets it; the access row;
 * then the answer. A person at the limit is refused every other case until midnight UTC, with nothing written, and every
 * staff account is told once that day.
 */
export async function readCase(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseView> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  const limits = await dailyLimits(deps.apiDb);
  const opened = await casesOpenedToday(deps.apiDb, session.userId, caseId);
  if (!opened.thisCase && opened.cases >= limits.caseOpens) {
    deps.background.start(() => alertDailyReads(deps, session.userId, limits.caseOpens));
    throw new ModerationError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()));
  }
  await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "case_opened" });
  return caseView(deps, session, row);
}

/**
 * The case as the answer to a decision the person's key has just confirmed on it (3c design, section 7.5, step 4): the
 * read is written to the access log like every read of a case, and it is not held to the day's limit on different
 * cases, which counts openings. A decision's answer is no opening of another case: its person has just acted on this
 * one, and the decision's own caps bound how often that can be. So no committed decision is answered with a refusal.
 */
export async function readDecidedCase(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseView> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "case_opened" });
  return caseView(deps, session, row);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- images in the console

/**
 * GET /api/staff/cases/:case/media/:media/:size: an image of the case's own post, opened for staff, or image_refused. The
 * media module's one function decides what may be opened at all (gate V: never a sealed or an erased image, never an
 * image of a frozen post, on whatever case, open or closed); this route adds that the image is the case's. In this order:
 *   1. the recusal check and the case, as on every case route; only a post's case shows images;
 *   2. the image is one that a snapshot of the case lists, while that snapshot still holds its content: read from the
 *      module's own evidence, before the media module is asked. An id that names nothing and an id of another post's image
 *      are then refused by the same steps, with no file looked for, so the time an answer takes tells the two apart no
 *      more than the answer does;
 *   3. the media module's answer, and that the image it opened is on the case's own post.
 * Every refusal reads the same, and the file's handle is closed on each refusal after the open. Each view is written to
 * the access log before a byte is sent. The caller streams the file and closes it.
 */
export async function caseImage(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string, mediaId: string, size: MediaSize): Promise<StoredFile> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  if (row.targetType !== "post") throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  // The id in the spelling the database writes, which is the one a snapshot lists its images by.
  const imageId = mediaId.toLowerCase();
  if (!(await snapshotListsImage(deps.apiDb, caseId, imageId))) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  const image = await deps.media.staffImage(imageId, size);
  if (!image) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  try {
    // The image is of another post than this case's: the same answer as for an image that is not shown at all.
    if (image.postId !== row.targetId) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
    await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "image_viewed", mediaId: imageId });
  } catch (err) {
    await image.file.handle.close();
    throw err;
  }
  return image.file;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- a fresh snapshot

/** The longest one run of the snapshot route waits for a lock: the post's row or the case's, which a decision holds while it is recorded. */
const SNAPSHOT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** Whether a stored snapshot holds exactly what a capture holds now. */
function sameContent(stored: SnapshotRead, live: SnapshotContent): boolean {
  const images = (list: SnapshotContent["media"]) => JSON.stringify((list ?? []).map((image) => [image.id, image.alt, image.width, image.height]));
  return (
    stored.authorHandle === live.authorHandle &&
    stored.postState === live.postState &&
    stored.postCreatedAt === live.postCreatedAt &&
    stored.replyToId === live.replyToId &&
    stored.quoteOfId === live.quoteOfId &&
    stored.body === live.body &&
    (stored.media === null) === (live.media === null) &&
    images(stored.media) === images(live.media) &&
    stored.displayName === live.displayName &&
    stored.bio === live.bio &&
    stored.handle === live.handle
  );
}

/**
 * How often the snapshot's transaction is run again after a deadlock or a lock timeout, as an intake's is: in each run
 * that gave way nothing was written.
 */
const SNAPSHOT_RETRIES = 3;

/**
 * POST /api/staff/cases/:case/snapshots: a fresh snapshot of the target as it stands, taken the intake's way (a post under
 * a share lock with its images under their row locks, held for the case; a tombstone for a deleted post; no content after
 * an erasure), when it differs from the case's newest one or that one is withheld or erased. It answers the new
 * snapshot's id and digest, or the newest one's when nothing differed, never content: the console reads the case again,
 * so every read of a case's content goes through that route's access row and the day's limit. It needs no key: it changes
 * nothing a user sees, and enters the record only through a decision that names it.
 *
 * Its locks come in another order than a decision's. An intake takes its case first, through its item; this route has no
 * row to store before the copy, and the API role, which holds no UPDATE on cases, cannot lock a case's row itself. So the
 * post is locked first, and the case's row only by the foreign key of a hold or of the snapshot's own row. A decision
 * takes the case and then its post: the two can wait for each other, and PostgreSQL then makes one give way. Like an
 * intake, the transaction is run again on a deadlock and on a lock timeout, up to three times, and when the last run
 * fails the same way the answer is case_closed: the case would not hold still, and the person tries again.
 */
export async function takeSnapshot(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "social" | "media">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<StaffSnapshotTaken> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => snapshotIn(deps, tx, row));
    } catch (err) {
      if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
      if (attempt >= SNAPSHOT_RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("case_closed");
    }
  }
}

/** One run of the snapshot's transaction: the copy of the case's target, compared with the newest snapshot and stored when it differs. */
async function snapshotIn(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "social" | "media">, tx: DbTx, row: CaseRow): Promise<StaffSnapshotTaken> {
  const caseId = row.id;
  await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${SNAPSHOT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
  // The transaction's start, which the snapshots' trigger stamps and the digest covers.
  const takenAt = await snapshotTime(tx);
  let content: SnapshotContent;
  if (row.targetType === "post") {
    const post = await deps.social.capturePost(tx, row.targetId);
    if (!post) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
    const held = await deps.media.hold(tx, [{ caseId, postId: row.targetId }]);
    content = {
      caseId,
      targetType: "post",
      targetId: row.targetId,
      authorHandle: post.authorHandle,
      postState: post.state,
      postCreatedAt: post.createdAt.toISOString(),
      replyToId: post.replyToId,
      quoteOfId: post.quoteOfId,
      body: post.body,
      media: held.get(row.targetId) ?? [],
      displayName: null,
      bio: null,
      handle: null,
    };
  } else {
    const profile = await deps.social.captureProfile(tx, row.targetId);
    if (!profile) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
    content = {
      caseId,
      targetType: "account",
      targetId: row.targetId,
      authorHandle: profile.handle,
      postState: null,
      postCreatedAt: null,
      replyToId: null,
      quoteOfId: null,
      body: null,
      media: null,
      displayName: profile.displayName,
      bio: profile.bio,
      handle: profile.handle,
    };
  }
  const [newest] = await caseSnapshots(tx, caseId, true);
  if (newest && !newest.withheld && !newest.erased && sameContent(newest, content)) return { id: newest.id, digest: newest.digest };
  return storeSnapshot(tx, takenAt, content);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- a moderator's own finding

/**
 * POST /api/staff/findings: opens a case, or joins the target's open one, on the moderator's own finding under a rule. It
 * runs the transaction every intake runs. A finding needs no key, but it has lasting effects (holds, possibly the urgent
 * lane; citing R2 it freezes what its case reaches and makes the final decision an admin's), so one staff account opens
 * at most the day's limit of them, counted before anything is written, and the home screen lists each account's count.
 *
 * Which targets are live is the one rule of every intake: citing R2, a post in any state and an account also under a
 * handle it has left; under any other rule, only a post its author has not deleted and an account that holds the handle
 * now. A target with nothing live is not_found, and nothing is written: a finding is never stored as answered at once.
 *
 * The target is resolved first, before the day's count is read: a link that names nothing, or another site, is answered
 * as that on any day, and only a finding that could be opened meets the limit.
 */
export async function openFinding(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, request: FindingRequest): Promise<FindingResponse> {
  const { target } = request;
  let named: NamedTarget;
  if (target.kind === "post") named = { type: "post", id: target.id, mediaId: target.mediaId ?? null };
  else if (target.kind === "account") named = { type: "account", handle: target.handle };
  else {
    const parsed = parseLink(deps.config.APP_ORIGIN, target.url);
    named = parsed.type === "post" ? { type: "post", id: parsed.id, mediaId: null } : parsed;
  }
  const suspect = request.ruleId === "R2";
  const found = await liveTarget(deps, named, suspect);
  if (!found) throw new ModerationError("not_found");

  const limits = await dailyLimits(deps.apiDb);
  if ((await findingsOpenedToday(deps.apiDb, session.userId)) >= limits.findings) {
    throw new ModerationError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()));
  }

  // A finding alleges no illegality and holds no text of its own: what the moderator writes is a saved text.
  const ground: IntakeGround = {
    kind: "finding",
    channel: "staff",
    reporterId: null,
    findingBy: session.userId,
    contactId: null,
    ruleId: request.ruleId,
    allegesIllegal: false,
    csam: false,
    category: request.category,
    categoryKeyword: null,
    citedLaw: null,
    explanation: null,
    bonaFide: false,
  };
  const live: LiveTarget = named.type === "post" ? { type: "post", id: found.id, position: 1, mediaId: named.mediaId } : { type: "account", id: found.id, position: 1, namedHandle: named.handle };
  const recorded = await recordIntake(deps, { ground, live: [live] });
  const item = recorded.items.find((candidate) => candidate.position === 1);
  if (!item || item.caseId === null) throw new Error("a finding's item was stored without a case");

  // A finding that puts an item into the urgent lane alerts staff as a notice does, after the commit and unwaited for.
  if (recorded.items.some((candidate) => candidate.caseId !== null && candidate.lane === 0)) {
    deps.background.start(async () => {
      await alertUrgentLane(deps);
    });
  }
  return { caseId: item.caseId };
}

/** An expected failure of a moderation flow. The HTTP layer turns it into an ErrorEnvelope with this code and status. */
export class ModerationError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: ModerationErrorKind,
    readonly status: ModerationErrorStatus = STATUS[code],
    message: string = MESSAGES[code],
    /** Set for rate_limited so the response can carry Retry-After. */
    readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number,
    /** 3f: the one refusal that carries a member, order_exists, names the order that stands (section 10.6). */
    readonly details?: unknown,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ModerationError";
  }

export function moderationErrorMessage(code: ModerationErrorKind): string {
  return MESSAGES[code];
}

/** Whether a message the database raised is one of the module's codes, which the triggers raise as their message. */
export function isModerationErrorCode(message: string): message is ModerationErrorCode {
  return ModerationErrorCode.safeParse(message).success;
}

/**
 * The work a request starts and does not wait for: the mails after a report or a notice (3c design, section 7.1, step
 * 5). The answer, which carries the reference and the token, must never wait for a relay. Every task's error is caught
 * and logged here, and the tasks are kept until they end, so that `settle` can wait for them all.
 */
export interface Background {
  start(task: () => Promise<void>): void;
  /** Resolves once every started task has ended, those started meanwhile included. */
  settle(): Promise<void>;
}

export function createBackground(log: Logger): Background {
  const running = new Set<Promise<void>>();
  return {
    start(task) {
      const run = (async () => {
        try {
          await task();
        } catch (err) {
          log.error({ err }, "moderation: a task started after a request failed");
        }
      })();
      running.add(run);
      void run.then(() => running.delete(run));
    },
    async settle() {
      while (running.size > 0) await Promise.all([...running]);
    },
  };
}

export interface ModerationDeps {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The auth module's interface: the human check, a notifier's contact and every mail. The module never sees an address. */
  auth: AuthForModeration;
  /** The social module's interface: the locks on profile rows and the reads evidence is copied from. */
  social: SocialForModeration;
  /** The media module's interface: an intake's holds on image rows, which this module never names itself. */
  media: MediaForCases;
  /** The shared limit store: what one sender may send, and the throttles of the staff alerts. */
  limits: RateLimitStore;
  /** The tasks requests started and did not wait for. */
  background: Background;
  config: Config;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
}

import { releaseNotices } from "./release";

/**
 * The dispatch job (3c design, sections 7.8 and 7.12): every ten minutes it repeats the staff alerts that are still due,
 * runs the daily release once its hour has come, sends the receipts and statements a relay failure left pending, mails
 * each address and account one update of the outcomes released to it, and gives up what stayed unsent for five days.
 *
 * A round runs its steps in the order 5, 3, 1, 2, 4, 6 of the design's list: the alerts first, and the daily release,
 * which writes only to the databases, before any mail, so it never waits behind a relay. Every step runs in a try of its
 * own, and so does every mail: a failure is logged with the step and the row's id, never an address, and leaves the row
 * as it was, so a row that keeps failing never stops the alerts, the release or another row's mail. It stays pending
 * until the last step gives it up.
 *
 * Every time the job compares is its own clock's (`deps.now()`), handed to the database as a parameter, so one clock
 * decides what is fifteen minutes or five days old, and a test can move it.
 */

const MINUTE_MS = 60_000;
const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * MINUTE_MS;

/** The job's name: its lock is `job:moderation-dispatch`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const DISPATCH_JOB = "moderation-dispatch";
/** The time between the end of one round and the start of the next. */
export const DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * MINUTE_MS;
/** A receipt, a statement and an urgent item are the job's once they are this old: until then the request that made them is still at work on them. */
const DUE_AFTER_MS = 15 * MINUTE_MS;
/** How many pending receipts one round sends. */
const RECEIPTS_PER_ROUND = 100;
/**
 * How many suspect cases one round asks the media module what they reach: one query a case, and a report of child sexual
 * abuse material needs no account, so a flood of them could hold the round's first step for minutes. The oldest cases
 * are read first; any beyond this count as calling, unread, which only repeats an alert that a case read later may ask for
 * anyway.
 */
export const URGENT_REACH_PER_ROUND = 200;
/** How long a cut-off's marker is kept: two days, so a marker is still there for every round of its own day. */
const MARKER_TTL_MS = 2 * DAY_MS;
/** How long the question "is the marker set?" holds the key when the process dies between asking and letting go. */
const MARKER_PROBE_MS = 30_000;

/** The key and the window of the queue-age alert. */
export const WAITING_ALERT_KEY = "moderation-waiting";
export const WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS = DAY_MS;

/** A round's cut-off: the latest dispatch hour (UTC) at or before the round's start. */
export function cutoffOf(start: Date, hour: number): Date {
  const today = Date.UTC(start.getUTCFullYear(), start.getUTCMonth(), start.getUTCDate(), hour);
  return new Date(today <= start.getTime() ? today : today - DAY_MS);
}

/**
 * The marker of a cut-off's release, by the cut-off's day and hour. Because the key holds the hour, a changed dispatch
 * hour gives a cut-off whose release has not run. It lives beside the jobs' locks, which a restore of the database does
 * not bring back: the README's restore steps delete the markers.
 */
export const dispatchMarkerKey = (cutoff: Date) => `moderation-dispatched:${cutoff.toISOString().slice(0, 13)}`;

/** What one round did, for its log line and for the tests. */
export interface DispatchReport {
  /** The urgent lane's repeat: what became of the alert, or "none" when no item still calls for someone. */
  urgent: "sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "nothing_waiting" | "none";
  /** The queue-age alert: what became of it, or "none" when no case is past its time. */
  waiting: "sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "none";
  /** How many items the daily release changed, or null when it did not run in this round. */
  released: number | null;
  /** Whether the cut-off's release, both halves, has finished: before this round or in it. */
  marked: boolean;
  /** Whether this round ran the release to its end and wrote the cut-off's marker itself: the daily round. */
  daily: boolean;
  /** The receipts and the statements whose result this round recorded. */
  receipts: number;
  statements: number;
  /** The addresses' contacts and the accounts whose update the relay took. */
  outcomeMails: number;
  givenUp: { receipts: number; authorMails: number; outcomes: number };
  /** 3f: the decisions the release of held notices told in this round. */
  noticesReleased: number;
  /** 3d Task 1: the authors told in this round that korbat lost the files of an image of theirs. */
  lostNotices: number;
  /** 3d Task 2: the authors told in this round of a release of sealed images of theirs. */
  releaseNotices: number;
}

/** What a mail's result is recorded as; nothing is recorded where the relay could not take the mail, so the next round sends it again. */
const RECORDED: Record<NotifierUpdateResult | AccountMailResult, MailState | null> = {
  sent: "sent",
  suppressed: "suppressed",
  no_address: "no_address",
  // A contact the janitor has forgotten has no address any more.
  forgotten: "no_address",
  // The relay refused the address for good: no later try changes that.
  refused: "failed",
  unavailable: null,
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 5: the alerts

/**
 * Whether an unanswered item of the urgent lane still calls for someone (3c design, section 7.12), in its three cases.
 *   1. A suspect item whose case reaches an image that is still served: until a choice not to seal is recorded on the
 *      case after the item arrived, and then only while no post with a served image was created after the newest such
 *      choice. Nothing else ends it short of the item's answer: after a note, a withhold or a field reset some reader, the
 *      uploader included, is still served the images. A seal ends it by leaving no served image.
 *   2. A suspect item whose case reaches no served image: until a decision taken while deciding, a note or a recorded
 *      choice not to seal comes after the item arrived.
 *   3. Any other item: while no decision taken while deciding came after it and, when the case is about an account or its
 *      post is not visible, no note did either. On a visible post a note never ends it: the post is withheld or decided.
 * The two times of case 1 are compared to the millisecond, and a post created in the same millisecond as the recorded
 * choice counts as created after it: the alert errs on the side of repeating.
 */
export function stillCalls(item: UrgentItemRow, reach: { served: number; newestServedAt: Date | null } | null): boolean {
  if (item.suspect) {
    if (reach === null) throw new Error("a suspect item is judged by what its case reaches");
    if (reach.served > 0) {
      if (!item.declinedAfter || item.newestDeclinedMs === null) return true;
      return reach.newestServedAt !== null && reach.newestServedAt.getTime() >= item.newestDeclinedMs;
    }
    return !(item.interimAfter || item.noteAfter || item.declinedAfter);
  }
  const noteCounts = item.targetType === "account" || item.postHidden;
  return !item.interimAfter && !(noteCounts && item.noteAfter);
}

/**
 * The open cases that hold an unanswered item of the urgent lane which is older than 15 minutes and still calls for
 * someone. What a case reaches is read once for a case, and only for a case that holds a suspect item, for at most
 * `limit` cases, the oldest first. An alert fails open: a case whose reach cannot be read counts as calling, and the
 * failure is logged with the case's id, so one case that keeps failing never silences the lane; so does a suspect case
 * beyond the limit, unread.
 */
export async function casesCalling(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log">, now: Date, limit = URGENT_REACH_PER_ROUND): Promise<string[]> {
  const items = await urgentItems(deps.apiDb, new Date(now.getTime() - DUE_AFTER_MS));
  const reaches = new Map<string, { served: number; newestServedAt: Date | null }>();
  const calling = new Set<string>();
  // Every read counts toward the limit, one that fails too.
  let reads = 0;
  for (const item of items) {
    if (calling.has(item.caseId)) continue;
    let reach = reaches.get(item.caseId) ?? null;
    if (item.suspect && reach === null) {
      if (reads >= limit) {
        calling.add(item.caseId);
        continue;
      }
      reads++;
      try {
        reach = await deps.media.reach({ type: item.targetType, id: item.targetId });
      } catch (err) {
        deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "urgent", caseId: item.caseId }, "moderation-dispatch: what a case reaches could not be read; the case counts as calling");
        calling.add(item.caseId);
        continue;
      }
      reaches.set(item.caseId, reach);
    }
    if (stillCalls(item, reach)) calling.add(item.caseId);
  }
  return [...calling];
}

/** The urgent lane's repeat: while a case still calls, the alert is sent again under the key and window of the first one. */
async function repeatUrgent(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date): Promise<DispatchReport["urgent"]> {
  if ((await casesCalling(deps, now)).length === 0) return "none";
  return alertUrgentLane(deps);
}

/**
 * The queue-age alert, at most once a day: per lane the cases past its response time with the oldest one's time, the
 * open cases that have held a measure taken while deciding for more than a day, whose author cannot appeal it, and (3e,
 * section 7.14) the replies to a suspension or a termination unanswered for longer than REPLY_AIM_HOURS, under the same
 * key and window: a reply before the start holds the suspension until someone answers it.
 */
async function alertWaiting(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date): Promise<DispatchReport["waiting"]> {
  const waiting = await waitingCases(deps.apiDb, now);
  if (waiting.lanes.length === 0 && waiting.interim === 0 && waiting.replies === null) return "none";
  // 3f's review (people4): the mail says whether the staff phones got the push, or that it is the only reminder.
  return staffAlert(deps, WAITING_ALERT_KEY, WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, { template: "moderation_waiting", lanes: waiting.lanes, interim: waiting.interim, replies: waiting.replies, phones: deps.config.NOTIFY !== "off" });
}

/**
 * 3e (design, sections 5 and 7.14 item 3): gives up the statement mails of decisions that hold an announced suspension
 * or termination, each alone, in a transaction that takes the decision's row while its mail is owed, then the subject's
 * profile FOR NO KEY UPDATE, then records the give-up: the mail's outcome fixes the measure's start, which the database
 * derives into the profile's columns, so the profile is held when it is recorded, and an on-time reply that holds the
 * profile is read before the start is derived. The order is sendStatement's (3e's review, database3), so the two never
 * take the same rows in opposite orders. Answers the ids given up; a failure for one is logged with the decision's id and
 * leaves it for the next round.
 */
export async function giveUpAnnounced(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "social" | "log">, now: Date): Promise<string[]> {
  const gone: string[] = [];
  for (const due of await announcedMailsDue(deps.apiDb, now, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays)) {
    try {
      const given = await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await beginMailRecord(tx);
        if (!(await lockPendingAuthorMail(tx, due.decisionId))) return false;
        await deps.social.lockAccounts(tx, [due.subjectId], "no key update");
        return giveUpAnnouncedMail(tx, due.decisionId);
      });
      if (given) gone.push(due.decisionId);
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "give-up", decisionId: due.decisionId }, "moderation-dispatch: an announced measure's mail could not be given up; it is tried again next round");
    }
  }
  return gone;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 3: the daily release

/**
 * Whether the marker is set. The lock a job runs under is also the store of its markers, and it can only take a key or
 * let it go: the question takes the key for a moment, which fails when the marker is there, and lets it go again. A
 * process that dies in between leaves the key for half a minute, not for the marker's two days.
 */
async function markerSet(lock: JobLock, key: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const probe = randomBytes(16).toString("hex");
  if (!(await lock.acquire(key, probe, MARKER_PROBE_MS))) return true;
  await lock.release(key, probe);
  return false;
}

/**
 * The daily release, until the cut-off's marker is set. (a) The database releases every item answered before the cut-off
 * and every changed outcome. (b) Every contact whose notice is still owed something is kept for another six months. The
 * marker is set once both have finished, so a round that fails in between runs the step again: the release then releases
 * nothing new, and no outcome mail goes before (b) has moved each contact's day.
 *
 * When the marker cannot be asked for, the step runs: it only repeats what a finished release leaves as it is. The round
 * is the daily one only when its own write of the marker was accepted. A marker that could not be written is logged, and
 * the next round that can write it is the daily one: a receipt that rides alone goes out once a day, never once a round.
 */
async function dailyRelease(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock, now: Date, report: DispatchReport): Promise<void> {
  const cutoff = cutoffOf(now, deps.config.MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR);
  const key = dispatchMarkerKey(cutoff);
  try {
    if (await markerSet(lock, key)) {
      report.marked = true;
      return;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker could not be read; the release runs again");
  }
  report.released = await releaseOutcomes(deps.apiDb, cutoff);
  const owed = await contactsOwed(deps.apiDb);
  if (owed.length > 0) await deps.auth.forgetNotifierAfter(owed, appealDeadline(now));
  report.marked = true;
  try {
    report.daily = await lock.acquire(key, "done", MARKER_TTL_MS);
    if (!report.daily) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker was not taken; the next round runs the release again");
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker could not be set; the next round runs the release again");
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 4: the outcome mails

/**
 * One line of the daily update, from a released item (3c design, section 7.8, step 4, and section 5). The outcome's words
 * are the contracts' one composition, with the scope the status page gives the same item; the other fields say which of
 * the mail's sentences go with the line.
 */
export function updateLine(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "config">, row: OutcomeLineRow): NoticeUpdateLine {
  const outcome = row.shownOutcome as ItemOutcome;
  const noAction = outcome === "no_violation" || outcome === "not_evident";
  let scope: OutcomeWordsInput["scope"] = null;
  // 3e (7.11 item 7): an item whose decision retired the handle reads that in place of the display name and bio, and one
  // whose decision suspended or terminated the account at once reads ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.measure, which names nothing
  // of what the measure is or how long it lasts.
  if (row.targetType === "account") scope = row.suspect || row.sealed ? "account_suspect" : row.retired ? "account_retired" : row.measure ? "account_measure" : "account";
  else if (row.hasCase && !row.suspect && row.quotes) scope = "quote";
  // "No action for now": decided while nobody could open the post's images, on an item about a post that is not itself suspect.
  const unseen = noAction && row.decisionUnseen && row.targetType === "post" && !row.suspect;
  let rule: OutcomeWordsInput["rule"] = null;
  if (outcome === "restricted_rule") {
    // The rule in the wording of the rulebook the decision was made under.
    const found = row.ruleId === null || row.rulesVersion === null ? undefined : getRule(row.ruleId, row.rulesVersion);
    if (!found) throw new Error("the item's restriction names no rule of a rulebook korbat holds");
    rule = { id: found.id, title: found.title };
  }
  return {
    ref: row.ref,
    item: row.position,
    link: itemLink(deps, row),
    outcome: outcomeWords({ outcome, rule, suspect: row.suspect, sealed: row.sealed, unseen, noEffect: row.noEffect, scope }),
    reexamination: row.reexamines,
    changed: row.changed,
    // Only a moderator's decision to take no action can be examined again, once; an answer given with the images out of
    // sight does not spend that, also when it answered a re-examination.
    reexaminable: row.byDecision && noAction && !row.reexamined && (!row.reexamines || unseen),
    unseen,
    automatic: !row.hasCase,
  };
}

/** The log line of a mail that did not go: a relay that could not take it is expected and tried again; anything else is a fault to read. */
function logUnsent(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "log">, err: unknown, step: string, row: Record<string, string | string[]>): void {
  if (err instanceof MailUnavailable) deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step, ...row }, "moderation-dispatch: a mail was not sent; it stays pending for the next round");
  else deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step, ...row }, "moderation-dispatch: a row failed and was left as it was; the round goes on");
}

/**
 * The outcome mails: every released item whose mail is pending, whichever round released it.
 *   - Signed out, the lines go by contact to the auth module, which alone knows which contacts share an address and sends
 *     each address one update. A receipt the 24-hour cap folded rides with its contact's lines; in the daily round a
 *     contact with a folded receipt and nothing else is passed too, so its address gets an update of receipts alone. In
 *     later rounds a folded receipt goes only with its own contact's retried lines, so an address gets one update a day.
 *   - Signed in, they go as one update per account. An item whose reporter was forgotten has nobody to mail.
 * Each line and each carried receipt records its result only while it is still pending. Where the relay could not take a
 * mail nothing is recorded, and the next round sends it again. The rows a mail's result is recorded on are taken before
 * it is sent, in the transaction that records it (beginMailRecord): a database that cannot write refuses that, and
 * nothing is sent, so a line is never mailed round after round for want of a record. The signed-out updates are one call
 * to the auth module, which groups the contacts by address, so their rows are taken and recorded in one transaction,
 * each part's record in a savepoint of its own; each account's update has a transaction of its own.
 */
async function outcomeMails(deps: ModerationDeps, report: DispatchReport): Promise<void> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const rows = await pendingOutcomeLines(q);
  const folded = new Map<string, NoticeRow>((await foldedReceipts(q)).map((notice) => [notice.contactId!, notice]));

  // One part for each contact, which is one notice; one list for each account.
  const byContact = new Map<string, { ref: string; items: string[]; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }>();
  const byAccount = new Map<string, { items: string[]; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }>();
  const nobody: string[] = [];
  for (const row of rows) {
    let line: NoticeUpdateLine;
    try {
      line = updateLine(deps, row);
    } catch (err) {
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { itemId: row.id });
      continue;
    }
    if (row.contactId !== null) {
      const part = byContact.get(row.contactId) ?? { ref: row.ref, items: [], lines: [] };
      part.items.push(row.id);
      part.lines.push(line);
      byContact.set(row.contactId, part);
    } else if (row.reporterId !== null) {
      const update = byAccount.get(row.reporterId) ?? { items: [], lines: [] };
      update.items.push(row.id);
      update.lines.push(line);
      byAccount.set(row.reporterId, update);
    } else {
      nobody.push(row.id);
    }
  }

  // Signed out. The parts keep the order of their notices, so an address's update lists them as they were sent.
  const parts: NotifierUpdatePart[] = [];
  const carried = new Map<string, NoticeRow>();
  const withReceipt = async (contactId: string, part: { ref: string; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }): Promise<void> => {
    const notice = folded.get(contactId);
    if (!notice) {
      parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines });
      return;
    }
    try {
      const receipt = await receiptMessage(deps, notice);
      carried.set(contactId, notice);
      parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines, receipt: { ref: receipt.ref, receivedAt: receipt.receivedAt, items: receipt.items } });
    } catch (err) {
      // The receipt could not be built: the lines go without it, and it waits for the next daily round.
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { intakeId: notice.id });
      if (part.lines.length > 0) parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines });
    }
  };
  for (const [contactId, part] of byContact) await withReceipt(contactId, part);
  if (report.daily) {
    for (const [contactId, notice] of folded) if (!byContact.has(contactId)) await withReceipt(contactId, { ref: notice.ref, lines: [] });
  }
  if (parts.length > 0) {
    // A transaction that fails before its mail (its rows could not be taken) has sent nothing; the round goes on.
    await q.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await beginMailRecord(tx);
      // Every line's row and every carried receipt's notice, before anything is sent; what another sender recorded
      // meanwhile is left out of the mail.
      const locked = await lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx, [...byContact.values()].flatMap((part) => part.items));
      const sending: NotifierUpdatePart[] = [];
      for (const part of parts) {
        const notice = carried.get(part.contactId);
        if (notice && !(await lockPendingReceipt(tx, notice.id, true))) carried.delete(part.contactId);
        const items = byContact.get(part.contactId)?.items ?? [];
        const lines = part.lines.filter((_, index) => locked.has(items[index]!));
        const receipt = carried.has(part.contactId) ? part.receipt : undefined;
        if (lines.length > 0 || receipt) sending.push({ contactId: part.contactId, ref: part.ref, lines, ...(receipt ? { receipt } : {}) });
      }
      if (sending.length === 0) return;
      let results = new Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>();
      try {
        results = await deps.auth.mailNotifierUpdates(sending);
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contacts: String(sending.length) });
      }
      for (const part of sending) {
        const state = RECORDED[results.get(part.contactId) ?? "unavailable"];
        if (state === null) continue;
        try {
          await tx.transaction(async (sp) => {
            await recordOutcomeMails(sp, (byContact.get(part.contactId)?.items ?? []).filter((id) => locked.has(id)), state);
            const notice = carried.get(part.contactId);
            if (notice) await recordCarriedReceipt(sp, notice.id, state);
          });
          if (state === "sent") report.outcomeMails++;
        } catch (err) {
          logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contactId: part.contactId });
        }
      }
    }).catch((err: unknown) => logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contacts: String(parts.length) }));
  }

  // Signed in: one update per account, through the account's own address, each in a transaction of its own.
  for (const [accountId, update] of byAccount) {
    try {
      await q.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await beginMailRecord(tx);
        const locked = await lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx, update.items);
        const lines = update.lines.filter((_, index) => locked.has(update.items[index]!));
        if (lines.length === 0) return;
        const state = RECORDED[await deps.auth.mailAccount(accountId, { template: "notice_update", lines })];
        if (state === null) return;
        await recordOutcomeMails(tx, update.items.filter((id) => locked.has(id)), state);
        if (state === "sent") report.outcomeMails++;
      });
    } catch (err) {
      // The rows are the items: the account is the reporter, whom no log line names.
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { itemIds: update.items });
    }
  }

  // The reporter's link was forgotten with their account: there is nobody to mail.
  if (nobody.length > 0) await recordOutcomeMails(q, nobody, "no_address");
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the notices of lost images (3d)

/** How many lost images' notices one round takes at most; the rest wait for the next round. */
const LOST_NOTICES_PER_ROUND = 50;

/**
 * 3d Task 1 (design, sections 7.1, 7.14 and 7.15; W.8): the mail image_lost to each author whose image's files the
 * quarantine's record says are lost, once an image, recorded as a statement's mail is: a result the relay took or refused
 * for good is recorded, and a relay that could not take it leaves the notice pending for the next round, until the give-up
 * days of 3c have passed since the record, when it is given up. An image whose row or post is gone has nobody left to tell
 * (`none`). Answers how many were sent; a row that fails is logged by its image's id and left as it was.
 */
export async function lostImageNotices(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date): Promise<number> {
  let sent = 0;
  for (const lost of await deps.media.lostUntold(LOST_NOTICES_PER_ROUND)) {
    try {
      if (lost.ownerId === null || lost.postCreatedAt === null) {
        await deps.media.lostTold(lost.mediaId, "none");
        continue;
      }
      if (now.getTime() - lost.lostAt.getTime() > RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays * DAY_MS) {
        await deps.media.lostTold(lost.mediaId, "failed");
        deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "image_lost", id: lost.mediaId }, "moderation: mail given up");
        continue;
      }
      const state = RECORDED[await deps.auth.mailAccount(lost.ownerId, { template: "image_lost", postCreatedAt: lost.postCreatedAt })];
      if (state === null) continue;
      await deps.media.lostTold(lost.mediaId, state);
      if (state === "sent") sent++;
    } catch (err) {
      logUnsent(deps, err, "notices", { mediaId: lost.mediaId });
    }
  }
  return sent;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the round

/**
 * One round. `lock` is the store the job's own lock lives in, where the daily release keeps its markers.
 */
export async function dispatchRound(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock): Promise<DispatchReport> {
  const now = deps.now();
  const report: DispatchReport = {
    urgent: "none",
    waiting: "none",
    released: null,
    marked: false,
    daily: false,
    receipts: 0,
    statements: 0,
    outcomeMails: 0,
    givenUp: { receipts: 0, authorMails: 0, outcomes: 0 },
    noticesReleased: 0,
    lostNotices: 0,
    releaseNotices: 0,
  };
  const step = async (name: string, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: name }, "moderation-dispatch: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };
  const due = new Date(now.getTime() - DUE_AFTER_MS);

  // 5. The alerts, each in a try of its own: a case whose reach cannot be read never holds the queue-age alert back.
  await step("urgent", async () => {
    report.urgent = await repeatUrgent(deps, now);
  });
  await step("waiting", async () => {
    report.waiting = await alertWaiting(deps, now);
  });

  // 3. The daily release.
  await step("release", () => dailyRelease(deps, lock, now, report));

  // 1. The receipts a relay failure left pending. sendReceipt records every result but a relay failure, which it logs
  // and leaves pending; any other fault it throws, and the row is logged here with the step and left as it was.
  await step("receipts", async () => {
    for (const intakeId of await pendingReceipts(deps.apiDb, due, RECEIPTS_PER_ROUND)) {
      try {
        const state = await sendReceipt(deps, intakeId);
        if (state !== "pending" && state !== "none") report.receipts++;
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "receipts", { intakeId });
      }
    }
  });

  // 3f (section 7.10): the release of held notices, before the statements, so that a notice told now is mailed in this
  // round. One transaction: the database's function, which tells what its hold no longer keeps and every decision held
  // with it, then, when it told anything, the audit row order_notices_released by the system, as its last statement.
  await step("order-notices", async () => {
    report.noticesReleased = await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
      const count = await releaseHeldNotices(tx);
      if (count > 0) {
        await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "order_notices_released", targetType: null, targetId: null, requestId: null, metadata: { count } });
      }
      return count;
    });
  });

  // 3d Task 1 (sections 7.1 and 7.14): the notices, before the statements. The authors whose image's files the
  // quarantine's record says are lost are mailed image_lost, once an image; the media module reads and records them
  // through lost_untold and lost_told, since the quarantine's table is closed to the API's role.
  await step("notices", async () => {
    report.lostNotices = await lostImageNotices(deps, now);
    // 3d Task 2 (sections 7.2 and 7.14): a release's notice that was born held goes pending in the round that finds the
    // last hold on telling ended, never earlier, and is mailed then; one the send after the commit left is mailed here.
    report.releaseNotices = await releaseNotices(deps, now, due, (err, row) => logUnsent(deps, err, "notices", row));
  });

  // 2. The statements that were not mailed after their decision's commit, as they are mailed there.
  await step("statements", async () => {
    for (const decisionId of await pendingAuthorMails(deps.apiDb, due)) {
      try {
        if ((await sendStatement(deps, decisionId)) !== "none") report.statements++;
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "statements", { decisionId });
      }
    }
  });

  // 4. The outcome mails, only once the cut-off's release has finished, so each contact's day was moved before its lines go.
  let outcomesTried = false;
  if (report.marked) {
    await step("outcomes", async () => {
      await outcomeMails(deps, report);
      outcomesTried = true;
    });
  }

  // 6. What stayed unsent for five days is given up, without another attempt. Outcome lines only in a round that tried
  // them, after it, so each is tried at least once even when the daily release kept failing for longer than that.
  await step("give-up", async () => {
    const gone = await giveUpReceiptsAndAuthorMails(deps.apiDb, now, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
    // 3e: the announced measures' statement mails, which the bulk statement leaves out, one by one under the profile's lock.
    const announced = await giveUpAnnounced(deps, now);
    report.givenUp.receipts = gone.receipts.length;
    report.givenUp.authorMails = gone.authorMails.length + announced.length;
    for (const id of gone.receipts) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "receipt", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
    for (const id of [...gone.authorMails, ...announced]) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "statement", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
    if (!outcomesTried) return;
    const lines = await giveUpOutcomeMails(deps.apiDb, now, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
    report.givenUp.outcomes = lines.length;
    for (const id of lines) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "outcome", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
  });

  // One line for a round that did something, so the day's release and its mails can be found in the log: counts only.
  const gaveUp = report.givenUp.receipts + report.givenUp.authorMails + report.givenUp.outcomes;
  if (report.daily || report.receipts + report.statements + report.outcomeMails + gaveUp + report.noticesReleased + report.lostNotices + report.releaseNotices > 0 || report.urgent === "sent" || report.waiting === "sent") {
    deps.log.info({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, ...report }, "moderation-dispatch: round");
  }
  return report;
}

/** The job: a round every ten minutes, counted from the end of the one before, on one API instance at a time. */
export function createDispatchJob(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: DISPATCH_JOB, intervalMs: DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => dispatchRound(deps, lock) });
}
